We’re looking for a **Senior Product Designer** to join ASquared. When we say senior, we mean someone with the experience, craft and judgement to take ownership of difficult product & design problems and move them forward.

You’ll be comfortable with ambiguity, strategic by nature, confident with clients and able to make excellent, informed decisions with little to no direction. You’ll know when to research, prototype, challenge, iterate and ship. And while strategy and systems thinking matters, so does your craft: you know how to combine interaction design, typography, hierarchy, visual design and great taste that turns a good idea into a genuinely great product.

## **What you’ll be doing**

Our work spans scaleups and established organisations but focuses primarily on exciting early-stage ventures through our **Impact Builder.** One day you might be helping a startup founder make sense of an early proposition, and the next you might be untangling a complex product with established users, technology and stakeholders.

In this role you’ll:

* **Own product design end-to-end.** From early user-centred discovery and understanding the problem through to polished, build-ready UI, and always working alongside engineers during delivery.
* **Turn ambiguity into direction.** You don’t need a perfect brief to get moving. Give you a messy problem, some constraints and the right people to talk to, and you’ll work out what needs to happen next.
* **Talk to humans.** You’re comfortable interviewing users and stakeholders, running testing sessions, finding the things people don’t necessarily put in the brief. Plus you’re able to communicate the process and value of design for those who might not realise it.
* **Run workshops that go somewhere.** Not workshops for the sake of workshops. You love to facilitate a room, ask good questions and drive people towards an outcome.
* **Make complicated things feel simple.** You’re strong across journeys, flows, information architecture and interaction design, and can untangle a genuinely difficult product problem rather than just make a straightforward one look beautiful.
* **Prototype to think.** You use sketches, wireframes and prototypes to quickly explore ideas, test assumptions and earn buy-in; and you know wireframes aren’t simply deliverables.
* **Care about the last 20%.** You’re a strong visual and UI designer with an eye for typography, hierarchy, layout and detail. You know when something is merely usable and when it actually feels good.
* **Work with engineers, not just hand work over to them.** You’ll stay involved through delivery, make pragmatic decisions when reality intervenes and help make sure what ships retains the quality of the thinking behind it.
* **Hold your own with clients.** You can explain and defend your decisions without hiding behind design jargon, accept feedback, challenge people constructively and change your mind when the evidence says you should.
* **Raise the bar around you.** You’ll give direct, useful critique, share what you know and help less experienced designers get better.
* 🤖🦾 Smart **AI workflows & tooling**. We expect you to be aware of the power of using AI in a design capacity, without letting it do your job for you. You use AI to accelerate research, exploration, prototyping and the wider product design process, and can demonstrate how you use it in your current workflows. But your judgement, and not the tool, is what really matters.

## **What we’re looking for**

You’ll probably have at least **6 years of professional product, UX or digital design experience** in an equivalent role, and are looking to take your next step. Rest assured we care considerably more about how you operate than the number on your CV.

We’d expect to see:

* A strong portfolio of **real, shipped digital products**, with real constraints and outcomes.
* End-to-end **product design experience** across research, UX, interaction and visual design.
* Excellent **design fundamentals** and a genuinely strong aesthetic sense.
* Strong Figma operator skills, including **prototyping, components and design systems**.
* Experience **working closely with engineers** and an understanding of how software actually gets built.
* Confidence **presenting** directly to, and working with, clients and senior stakeholders.
* The ability to **manage your own work**, priorities and communication without needing continual direction.

Agency or consultancy experience would be particularly useful as you’ll need to get up to speed with unfamiliar organisations and products quickly. Native mobile, SaaS, complex B2B or early-stage product experience would also be valuable.

### **What senior means at ASquared**

Senior doesn’t mean knowing everything or never asking for help. It means having the judgement to take responsibility for the work, and proactively know when to seek advice from others.

You can make decisions with incomplete information, disagree with a client without making the relationship difficult, defend good work without becoming precious about it, and ask for another perspective because it might make the work better.

### **Why ASquared?**

You’ll get the variety of studio life with real ownership, and get to work on projects that are truly impactful and interesting. As a B Corp we firmly believe in using Tech for Good. Plus you’ll work directly with founders, clients, users and engineers, often from the earliest conversations through to what actually gets built.

We’re a central Brighton-based digital product studio working across mobile apps, web products and digital platforms. We’re also the studio behind **Impact Builder**, our venture-building programme for purpose-led startups, and we’re a certified B Corp.

If you enjoy difficult problems, still care deeply about the craft and want meaningful autonomy without having to become a people manager, **we’d like to meet you.**

### **The practical stuff**

🔹 Flexible hybrid working. We spend **Tuesdays** and **Fridays** together at our Platf9rm office in Brighton as a team, with the option to work from home or Platf9rm the rest of the week  
🔹 Access to wellbeing resources including counselling, GP services and much more, via 360 Wellbeing  
🔹 Digital Nomad policy: work from anywhere in the world for up to a month per year, post-probation  
🔹 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing over time  
🔹 Extra day off for your birthday  
🔹 NEST pension  
🔹 Employee referral scheme (£500, subject to conditions)  
🔹 Monthly social events, team lunches, and networking opportunities  
🔹 Dog-friendly office. Bring your pooch along  
🔹 A blended team that wants someone senior enough to challenge them, not just agree with them

## **Applying**

Send us your **CV and portfolio**.

Your portfolio matters considerably more to us than how polished your CV is. We want to understand the problems you tackled, what **you** actually did, the decisions you made and why, where things changed, and what happened when the product reached users.

We don’t expect a portfolio full of perfect projects. An experienced designer who can talk clearly and candidly about the difficult ones is much more interesting.

Axelera AI is not your regular deep-tech company. We are creating the next-generation AI platform to support anyone who wants to help advancing humanity and improve the world around us.

**Position Overview**

As a Staff AI Application Engineer in the Model Enablement team (Application Software), you will build our model enablement platform and decide how each model runs across the Metis or Europa AIPU, the host CPU and the host's accelerators. How this work is split and scheduled determines most of the end-to-end performance a customer sees in the Voyager SDK.

The role combines architecture and hands-on work across the model frontend, the graph compiler, the runtime and the application pipeline. During model bring-up, you cover the frontend and graph side, and a device-side engineer covers the backend.

Our team uses AI coding agents in daily work, and you will use them to build, test and verify your own work. We also welcome experienced field application engineers, technical leads and engineering managers who want to return to hands-on engineering. Experience in planning, delegating and reviewing work transfers well to working with AI agents.

**Key responsibilities:**

* **Model enablement platform and agent harness:** Build the platform that engineers and AI agents use to bring up models: reusable tools to partition, compile, run and profile; environments with access to real hardware; closed-loop runs that apply a change, measure it against the reference and repeat; and verification (differential testing, regression detection) integrated into CI.
* **Model ingestion:** Own how a PyTorch or ONNX model is captured, analysed and split across the AIPU's matrix and RISC-V vector units, the host CPU and the host's accelerators (GPU, NPU, video decoder), with placement tags that users can read and override. Build this with the graph compiler team so it works for every model.
* **Heterogeneous execution:** Extend that split to large models, cascades and multi-model pipelines, for example with expert offloading and caching across device and host memory. Agree the plan with the graph compiler team.
* **End-to-end performance:** With the application team (pipeline builder) and the runtime team, bring each model to its best end-to-end performance: overlap of host and device work, zero-copy buffers, batching, multi-core scheduling, and models with several inputs. Profile device time, host time and data movement, and confirm each speedup in the full pipeline.
* **Critical models:** Study the models that matter most to customers, on Metis today and on Europa, and turn each lesson into a platform improvement.

**Qualifications:**

**Essential**

* 8+ years of engineering experience in systems, compilers, runtimes or performance, including system-level design ownership.
* Hands-on experience with heterogeneous computing across CPU, GPU, DSP, NPU or FPGA, including reasoning about compute, memory bandwidth, latency and data movement.
* Solid fundamentals in computer architecture, operating systems and parallel programming.
* Familiarity with ML graph representations and compiler concepts: graph capture (torch.export, FX, ONNX), lowering, operator fusion, partitioning, memory planning.
* Strong C++ and Python.
* Daily use of AI coding agents on real engineering work, with the judgment to review and test their output.

**Preferred**

* Hands-on experience with MLIR or another compiler framework (TVM, XLA, TorchInductor, IREE).
* Experience with an inference runtime or execution engine (ONNX Runtime execution providers, a custom NPU or DSP runtime).
* Experience with GPU compute (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan) or SIMD optimization on Arm or x86.
* Experience with large-model execution techniques such as offloading, expert caching, speculative decoding, pipelining across devices.
* Experience building agent environments, evaluation harnesses or verification frameworks (differential testing, regression detection), or MCP-based tooling.

# Independent Member, Financial Markets Infrastructure Committee (FMIC)

London, United Kingdom

## Job Description

**Introduction**

The Bank of England’s Court of Directors is seeking to appoint a new independent member to the Financial Market Infrastructure Committee (FMIC).

The Bank of England sits at the heart of the UK’s economy and financial system. Its mission is to promote the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability.

The FMIC was established as a statutory committee of the Bank under the Bank of England Act 1998 (as amended by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023). The FMIC governs the work of the Bank of England on financial market infrastructure encompassing supervision and policy for payment systems (including stablecoin), central counterparties and central securities depositories.  Its decisions play a crucial role in ensuring the resilience of the systems and markets on which both retail and wholesale users depend.  This is a particularly interesting time given the extent of technological change and innovation taking place across the FMI landscape and a unique opportunity to play a part in a once-in-a-generation modernisation of money and markets.  For more information on the FMIC’s work, see our most recent annual report available here (see here).

The coming period will see the FMIC – along with the Bank’s other policy committees – continue to deal with a wide range of issues. This will include assessing financial and operational risks to the resilience of FMIs and ensuring the Bank’s approach to supervision remains appropriate to the evolving market context. The Committee will continue to embed the new responsibilities of the Bank in relation to rulemaking and the secondary innovation objective through which the Bank seeks to facilitate innovation in the provision of FMI services.

The knowledge and analytical rigour that the independent members bring to bear on the Committee’s work, along with the challenge they provide, ensures that the FMIC’s decision making is robust and effective.

**Appointment description**

Key responsibilities of FMIC Members

• Providing independent challenge, perspective and insights across the breadth of the FMIC’s policymaking and supervisory remit.

• Contributing an understanding of the broader context to FMIC discussions.

• Providing oversight of the FMIC’s strategy and delivery.

**Organisation description**

The FMIC is accountable to Parliament and reports to it annually. The FMIC has several non-delegable responsibilities which include the Bank’s FMI related policy-making functions.

FMIC is chaired by the Governor or Deputy Governor for Financial Stability. Its other members consist of  4 Bank members (including the Bank’s Executive Director for FMI), and at least 3 (currently 4) independent members. The Committee meets regularly to take decisions on rules and on firm-specific issues. In addition, it sets the strategy and approach to supervision.

**Minimum criteria**

* **Strong and proven financial sector knowledge and experience at a senior level**– candidates must have the experience necessary to make independent decisions. They must demonstrate that they have used their financial sector expertise operating at a senior level in or in relation to financial services organisations, ideally financial market infrastructure firms.

**Essential criteria**

* **Decision-making skills** – the FMIC makes decisions that directly affect firms and people.  All members should have strong leadership skills, a strategic mindset, and be ready to take tough decisions and stand by them.

* **Analytical ability**– candidates will need to be able to absorb large volumes of complex information and reach reasoned and robust conclusions.

* **Independence of thought and interpersonal skills** – Candidates must be able to exert influence within the FMIC providing robust challenge whilst working closely and constructively with FMIC members.

* **Excellent communication skills**– the Bank has to communicate with firms, trade associations, civil society, ministers and relevant Parliamentary Committees. External members of the Committee can be called before the Treasury Committee in the Commons and the Financial Services Regulation Committee in the Lords (along with other members) to explain the FMIC’s policies.

* **Undisputed integrity and standing** – candidates should have no reservations about meeting the requirements of the Bank’s Code of Conduct and the Conflicts Code for the FMIC. An assessment of potential conflicts of interest will be undertaken as part of the selection process.

**Desirable criteria**

* An understanding of how regulation can enable responsible innovation and/or influence regulatory approaches in other jurisdictions.

* An understanding of how financial infrastructure firms effectively implement and maintain technology infrastructure, and the opportunities and risks that technological developments may pose for the industry and regulators.

* An understanding of how policy is developed and implemented, including the theory of regulation.

**Appointment terms**

Members will normally be appointed for a fixed term of 3years.  Members may typically serve no more than 2consecutive terms. Members will ultimately be accountable to Court.

**Conflicts of interest**

Members will be subject to FMIC’sconflicts-of-interest policy.  Applicants must declare any actual or potential conflicts before appointment and any conflicts that arise during their term. Candidates should therefore consider carefully whether their existing appointments, responsibilities or interests could affect, or reasonably be perceived to affect, their ability to serve on the committee.

---

Job Advert

Are you an experienced Administrator with an interest or experience in the Agricultural sector? Would you like to take your next step and develop your career as part of a well-established, pioneering UK property consultancy?

At Bidwells, our **Agriculture and Environment** team within our Rural Department are a leading provider of consultancy and management services to the farming, food, bioenergy and agri-investment sectors.  We have a proven track record and expertise spanning all aspects of the farming, food, energy and agri-investment sectors, providing a holistic approach advising at every level of the supply chain from life sciences and farming to food processing and retail.

An exciting new opportunity has arisen for a **Farm Administrator** to join our busy team and provide administrative and business support to the Agriculture & Environment consultants in our Cambridge office. In this role, you will help deliver farm management, contract farming and environmental services to a portfolio of client farming businesses and estates.

We are looking for enthusiastic, proactive candidates who have strong attention to detail, a numerical mind and an interest in farming, that can work well with colleagues and clients at all levels. We are open to considering full-time or part-time options for this role.

**What you’ll be doing**

* Farm business administration
  + Prepare and maintain farm and cropping records and collate sales information.
  + Use account software to extract and interpret financial data for performance analysis.
  + Process supplier invoices and help prepare/update budgets, cash flows and forecasts.
  + Liaise with clients, contractors and suppliers.
  + Prepare meeting packs as well as take and circulate minutes.
* Support applications and claims for farming schemes and grants, keeping track of deadlines, payments and relevant policy changes.
* Help maintain compliance records and develop knowledge of key farming and environmental schemes.
* Prepare and maintain farming agreements, licences and tenancies, ensuring key renewal and termination dates are effectively managed.
* Support senior consultants in providing management and strategic advice to farming and contracting businesses, including business plans and reports.
* Arrange and attend farm visits and client meetings, providing follow-up support and correspondence.
* Data management: Help capture and manage farm business data and produce reports for clients and consultants.
* Work in line with company standards, best practice and relevant legislation, maintaining high standards of quality and compliance.
* Maintain your professional and technical knowledge through ongoing development and share knowledge and best practice with colleagues.

**About you**

* Have an interest in or understanding of agriculture, land management or the rural economy.
* Strong administration skills. Any experience specifically in a similar farm or estate administration role or within a rural consultancy would be an advantage, but not essential.
* Good numeracy, with confidence working on budgets, invoices and financial data.
* Excellent organisational and administrative skills, with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
* Clear and confident written and verbal communication, including a professional telephone manner.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, stay calm under pressure and meet deadlines.
* Self-motivated, able to use their own initiative, and willing to take on new challenges.
* A positive, flexible team player
* Experience of introducing new ways of working to improve efficiency.
* Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel and Word.
* Familiarity with farm management and accounting software such as Farmplan Gatekeeper, Muddy Boots, Greentree and Key Prime would be a bonus.
* Any knowledge or experience of the Rural Payments service or agri-environment schemes would be useful but not essential.
* Full UK driving licence and own car.

**Why Bidwells?**

We’re a different kind of business. Whilst we’re a major player in the property sector, Bidwells remains a privately-owned, independent Partnership, with an inclusive, entrepreneurial culture. We give our people autonomy and take the time to listen. As a certified B Corporation (B-Corp), we are dedicated to using our business as a force for good, driving innovation, and creating long-term value for our clients, communities, and the environment.

**What’s in it for you**

**Competitive Salary:** We recognise and reward talent with generous salary and group bonus scheme. As a Real Living Wage employer, we’re committed to fair pay that reflects the true cost of living.

**Comprehensive Benefits:** Including up to 8% matched pension, 28 days holiday (+ bank holidays) as a minimum, along with your birthday off work, a wellness day, paid sabbaticals, private medical cover, medicash plan, lifestyle discounts and perks, and more.

**Professional Development:** Continuous learning, study support and promotion opportunities.

**Innovative Culture:** Be part of a forward-thinking team at the forefront of industry trends.

**Family Friendly:** We offer enhanced family leave policies to support individuals close to you.

**Work-Life Balance:** We value your well-being and offer agile working to support it.

*Bidwells is dedicated to fostering a truly inclusive culture of belonging, where everyone can thrive and succeed as their true and authentic selves at every level. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and positively encourage applications from all suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of race, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, disability, age, sexual orientation, transgender status, religion or belief. Flexible working requests are considered from day one.*

Recruitment agencies: Bidwells only pay agency fees where we have a signed agreement in place and that agency has been contacted and directed by a member of our Talent Acquisition Team to work on a specific vacancy. We do not pay agency fees when speculative and unsolicited CVs are submitted to Bidwells or any of our employees other than via our Applicant Tracking System and through our recruitment process. If this is not adhered to, agency fees will not be paid. Submission of any unsolicited CVs or proposals to Bidwells will be deemed evidence of full and unlimited acceptance of this approach.

# Forward Deployed Product Manager - AI Agent (EMEA)

# Job Description

Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day.

Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu, founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

**About the Role**

As our first EMEA **Forward Deployed Product Manager, AI Agent**, you will create, deploy and optimize AI Agents that transform our customers’ businesses and delight their customers. This highly cross-functional and customer-facing role blends product thinking, a nose for value, and project leadership with senior customer executives. At the end of the day, you own each AI Agent and the outcomes they drive for our customers, and you take that personally. You are a creative, pragmatic problem solver who thrives in fast-paced environments, rolls up your sleeves to build, and excels at turning ambiguity into execution.

In this role, you’ll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who will support the build, integrations and optimization to make each AI Agent successful. You’ll also work closely with product and engineering, providing a tight feedback loop and custom tooling that will shape the future of our platform. As the first hire in EMEA, you’ll also play a key role in setting the standards for the role in the EMEA region and helping to grow the team as we scale.

**What You’ll Do**

* **Own AI Agent outcomes for our customers** — defining and delivering on the metrics that move the needle. This includes finding additional automation opportunities that can provide even more value! To do this, you’ll...
* **Own the deployment lifecycle** for AI Agents — from scoping and kickoff to launch and post-go-live optimization
* **Design, build, test and iterate on AI agents** in partnership with FDEs using Cresta’s internal tools and the latest technologies to deliver the highest customer ROI
* **Serve as the AI Agent SME for the EMEA Sales cycle,** partnering on demos, solutioning, and deal reviews to ensure technical feasibility, value articulation, and successful handoff to deployment.
* **Lead customer relationships** and act as the primary point of contact for AI Agent. Help customers move faster to ensure we can deliver quickly and effectively.

# Police Community Support Officer (PCSO)

**Make a difference where it matters most**

Join British Transport Police as a Police Community Support Officer and play a vital role in protecting passengers, supporting communities and keeping the railway safe.

**Location:** Plymouth  
**Salary:** £29,483.96 per year  
**Shift Allowance:** Up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training  
**Annual Leave:**28 days, rising to 30 days with service

**Why become a BTP PCSO?**

Police Community Support Officers are an integral part of British Transport Police.

As a PCSO, you will provide a visible and reassuring presence across the railway network. You will engage with passengers, support railway staff, respond to local concerns and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Chief Superintendent David Rams explains:

*“Our PCSOs are an integral part of British Transport Police. They carry out vital work across the railway network to keep passengers and staff safe, delivering an exceptional service to our communities across England and Wales.”*

**The difference you will make**

As a BTP PCSO, you will help prevent crime, reduce disruption, support vulnerable people and build public trust and confidence across the railway network.

No two days will be the same. You will:

* Conduct visible patrols at stations and across the rail network
* Support victims and provide reassurance to passengers, railway staff and the public
* Assist with minor investigations and intelligence gathering
* Help manage security threats and operational incidents
* Build strong relationships with communities and partner organisations
* Work alongside Police Officers and other policing colleagues
* Help identify and respond to local concerns affecting the railway

**An enhanced operational role**

Unlike PCSOs in many Home Office police forces, BTP PCSOs are trained and equipped with handcuffs. This reflects the distinctive operational environment in which our PCSOs work and the important contribution they make to keeping the railway safe.

**What we are looking for**

We are looking for people who:

* Are resilient and able to remain calm under pressure
* Can communicate confidently with people from different backgrounds
* Demonstrate excellent customer service skills
* Have strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities
* Are committed to supporting communities and building trust
* Can use good judgement when responding to challenging situations
* Work effectively as part of a team
* Share our commitment to providing an excellent service to the public

You do not need previous policing experience to apply. We are interested in your values, motivation, transferable skills and potential to succeed in the role.

**What you will receive**

In return for the important work you undertake, you will receive:

* A salary of £29,483.96 per year
* A shift allowance of up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training
* 28 days’ annual leave, rising to 30 days with service
* Travel benefits
* Ongoing learning and professional development
* Access to in-house talent and development teams
* Career development opportunities across British Transport Police
* A defined contribution pension scheme administered by Royal London

**Develop your career with BTP**

A career as a Police Community Support Officer is rewarding and important in its own right.

PCSOs play a vital role in neighbourhood policing, safeguarding vulnerable people, solving problems within communities and building public trust and confidence across the railway network.

British Transport Police is committed to supporting your long-term development. You will have opportunities to broaden your knowledge, strengthen your operational skills and explore career development opportunities across the organisation.

If you later decide to pursue a career as a Police Constable, successful completion of your PCSO probationary period will also satisfy the work experience requirement for the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP).

This is one of several possible development opportunities available to you and does not diminish the importance or professional standing of the PCSO role.

**Working patterns**

Policing the railway requires flexibility.

You must be prepared to work shifts, including weekends and bank holidays. Further information about working patterns will be provided during the recruitment process.

**Before you apply**

You will not be eligible to apply if:

* You have been unsuccessful at interview for a BTP PCSO role within the last three months
* You have been unsuccessful at the application or online testing stage for a PCSO, Police Officer or Special Constable role within the last three months

Declaring a previous matter does not necessarily mean that your application will be unsuccessful. Each case will be considered individually.

**At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.**

  

As the world’s biggest medical research charity, we’ve helped bring eleven new cancer drugs to market. However, there is still an urgent need to bring more effective treatments to patients faster.

  

We have recently developed a new approach to driving therapeutic innovation through the creation of Cancer Research Horizons (CRH). We have brought together Cancer Research UK’s established drug discovery teams under one organisation and leadership team, combining our unique pipeline of cancer biology expertise and access to CRUK’s world-class academic network, cutting edge technology platforms and clinical expertise to 1) bring new treatments to patients faster and 2) tackle the biggest challenges in discovering cancer drugs by seeking out more radical ideas and embracing risk in our bid to achieve success.

  

Based at sites in Cambridge, the CRUK Scotland Institute in Glasgow and Newcastle University, Cancer Research Horizons employs ~180 staff from both industrial and academic backgrounds.

  

In this role you will support the overarching objective of CRH-TI to discover novel cancer therapeutic agents that will ultimately provide patient benefit. This will involve the prosecution of a laboratory-based project that is designed to expand the Medicinal Chemistry team’s technical capabilities.  
  
The successful candidate will join the Medicinal Chemistry team and will have an opportunity to apply their understanding of organic synthesis in our chemistry labs, working alongside an expert team of Medicinal Chemists.

* Development of greener and more sustainable chemistry techniques in our labs, such as electrochemistry and the use of green solvents.

Key duties will include:

  

* Assist with gathering, analysing and presenting information about our portfolio of early-phase drug development projects to support the effective review and management of the CDD portfolio e.g., project goal tracking and reporting.

* Support routine and targeted reviews of the CDD portfolio, creating/updating tools to gather and present information, coordinating provision and internal review of information and organising logistics for the review as needed.

* Support monthly management meetings (Portfolio Review Team, PRT) by writing minutes, preparing slides and performing other activities as needed.

* Assist with user account management for Portfolio Management/Dashboard tools.

* Ensure project information held in Portfolio Management/Dashboard tools are up to date, by reviewing data and prompting Project Leaders to update their project information.

* Update and maintain resource planning models to capture functional group resource forecasting across CDD and to coordinate information gathering across functional groups and project teams.

* Assist with developing data visualisation methods and tools for CDD portfolio information and maintain up to date information.

* Create, update and maintain models and trackers for the effective delivery of Portfolio activities and analyses.

* Support change initiatives both within Portfolio Management and across CDD including external benchmarking, stakeholder management and development and delivery of relevant training and guidance documents.

* Maintain a broad awareness of Portfolio Management practices and trends in the pharmaceutical sector and wider landscape.

* Create, update and maintain guidance documents for portfolio processes and tools

* Play a supportive role in contributing to and maintaining a cohesive Project and Portfolio Management function.

If you’re a motivated life sciences student, with an interest in drug development, data analysis and visualisation, and oncology clinical trials, then this is your opportunity to gain invaluable experience working within the pharmaceutical sector.

* Excellent organisational and interpersonal skills.

* Good teamwork skills.

* A meticulous eye for detail.

* Good time management skills.

* A sound knowledge of Microsoft packages.

* Familiarity with ICH/GCP guidelines is beneficial but not essential.

* Experience working in an office environment is beneficial but not essential.

**Our Mission**

We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. **About the Role**

As a Financial Services Disputes Lawyer, you will be responsible for leading the litigation strategy and managing a portfolio of consumer claims for Capital One. This portfolio mainly consists of residual PPI claims alongside a small number of other consumer claims. The role requires a highly strategic approach to handling litigation, including dealing with any threatened or issued group litigation and addressing any commercial disputes. Regular horizon scanning and preparing comprehensive reports for senior stakeholders on litigation trends will be essential parts of your remit to ensure the business is well prepared for emerging litigation risks. As well as engaging with any consultations which could impact the litigation landscape.

  

In addition to direct litigation management, you will play a critical advisory role for key first line operational functions. You will provide second-line support for section 75 Consumer Credit Act 1974 claims and disputed transactions, you will also be responsible for building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims. You will also provide second-line strategic support complaints, involving direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex and high-profile complaints.

  

**What you’ll do**

  

* **Lead Litigation & Strategy:** Manage a portfolio of consumer claims (primarily residual PPI and other ad-hoc claims), setting the overarching litigation strategies and proactive approaches to handle volumes and manage cases through to trial.
* **Group Litigation & Commercial Disputes:** Handle any threatened or issued group litigation effectively and efficiently, engaging and instructing external counsel on these claims where appropriate.
* **Commercial Contract Disputes:** Engaging with our contracts team where any commercial disputes arise, guiding them through any informal dispute resolution as well as dealing with any issued claims that may arise.
* **s.75 & Disputed Transactions:** Provide robust second-line support for the s.75 team and disputed transactions, including building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims.
* **Complaints Strategy:** Provide second-line support on the complaints strategy, including direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex, high-profile complaints.
* **Reporting & Horizon Scanning:** Conduct continuous horizon scanning to monitor key legal developments and litigation trends. Prepare reports and strategic updates for senior management.
* **External Engagement:** Manage external parties, including law firms and external counsel, to drive favourable outcomes.
* **Caseload Management:** Ensure compliance with court timetables, draft complex court documents, and conduct settlement negotiations.
* **Team Contribution:** Mentor junior team members and contribute to an engaging, inclusive, and high-performing team environment.

**The skills and experience you need**

  

* A qualified lawyer/solicitor with significant experience handling a caseload of consumer credit litigated claims and commercial disputes in private practice or an in-house legal team.
* Demonstrable experience dealing with s.75 claims, disputed transactions, and ideally building recovery strategies.
* Experience handling complex complaints and engaging effectively with Claims Management Companies (CMCs).
* Proven track record in setting and executing litigation strategies and experience with group litigation.
* Exceptional drafting skills for correspondence, strategic advice notes, and formal court documents.
* Strong legal research and horizon-scanning skills to preemptively identify risks.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities effectively and decisively.
* Demonstrates excellent judgment and problem solving capabilities.
* Proactive ownership of key tasks with excellent stakeholder management, reporting, and appropriate escalation.
* Results-focused and receptive to feedback, with a desire to own and drive continuous development.

Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. At our Nottingham head office, you'll find an on-site gym, restaurant and dedicated Learning Loft. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.

United Kingdom - Remote

# Security Engineer, Governance, Risk & Compliance (EMEA)

## The role:

GRC work is at its best when it makes security clearer, more consistent, and easier to operate. As a Security Engineer focused on Governance, Risk & Compliance, you’ll help maintain and improve Chainguard’s compliance and risk programs while building the experience and judgment to take on broader ownership over time.

You’ll work closely with experienced security and GRC partners to support SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 audit readiness, keep evidence and controls organized, help manage risk and remediation work, and improve the systems and processes behind our compliance program.

This is an earlier-career, hands-on role. You don’t need to have led an audit or built a GRC function before. We’re looking for someone with strong organizational habits, good judgment, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. You’ll have clear areas of responsibility, regular opportunities to work cross-functionally, and support from teammates as you grow your expertise.

Chainguard is building the secure foundation for software development and deployment. You’ll contribute to that mission by helping our security practices remain effective, measurable, and worthy of our customers’ trust.

## What you’ll do:

* Support audit readiness activities for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and other security assurance initiatives.
* Coordinate evidence collection with teams across Security, Engineering, Legal, HR, Product, and other functions.
* Help maintain security policies, standards, procedures, control descriptions, and supporting documentation.
* Assist with control testing, risk assessments, gap analysis, and remediation tracking.
* Keep compliance and risk information accurate and up to date in GRC platforms such as Vanta.
* Help translate auditor, customer, and internal security requests into clear next steps for the right stakeholders.
* Track action items, follow up on dependencies, and communicate status, risks, and blockers clearly.
* Identify opportunities to simplify and improve GRC workflows through better documentation, automation, and use of modern tooling.
* Develop and maintain repeatable processes, checklists, runbooks, and evidence-collection practices.
* Support customer security reviews, questionnaires, and third-party risk activities as needed.
* Learn Chainguard’s systems and security practices well enough to ask useful questions, identify inconsistencies, and escalate potential risks with clear context.
* Partner with senior members of the Security and Governance, Risk & Compliance teams on projects that improve Chainguard’s security posture.

## What we’re looking for:

* 2+ years of experience in information security, GRC, compliance, audit, risk, IT, or a related field; equivalent practical experience is welcome.
* Experience supporting audits, control activities, risk assessments, security questionnaires, or compliance programs.
* Strong organizational and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage details across multiple workstreams.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain requests and findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* A structured, detail-oriented approach to documentation, evidence management, and follow-through.
* Curiosity about how technology and security controls work, with the confidence to ask questions and investigate unfamiliar topics.
* Comfort working with spreadsheets, documentation systems, ticketing tools, and GRC platforms.
* An interest in improving repetitive processes through automation, better tooling, or clearer workflows.
* A collaborative, team-first approach and the ability to work effectively with colleagues across regions and functions.
* Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities and processes continue to evolve.

## Nice to have:

* Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, or another security or assurance framework.
* Familiarity with GRC platforms such as Vanta, Drata, or similar tools.
* Experience with control testing, risk registers, remediation plans, or policy management.
* Exposure to cloud environments, SaaS applications, software development practices, or security operations.
* Familiarity with third-party risk management or customer security reviews.
* Experience improving workflows with automation, integrations, or lightweight scripting.

## Why you’ll love it here:

We take security seriously without making it unnecessarily complicated. At Chainguard, you’ll:

* **Learn by doing:** Work on real security and assurance programs with support from experienced teammates.
* **Challenge the status quo:** Help simplify processes, improve tooling, and find better ways to get important work done.
* **Collaborate across borders:** Partner with colleagues across EMEA and the broader Chainguard organization.
* **Grow your scope:** Build the technical judgment and program-management skills needed to take on increasingly complex security initiatives.
* **Win together:** We share context, assume good intentions, and value collective success over individual heroics.
* **Bring your whole self:** We do serious work, but we also believe humor, curiosity, and enjoying the people you work with make the work better.

Base Salary Range

$89,000 - $105,000 USD

### About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

* We are customer obsessed — We focus on delivering solutions to our customers that create value and make their lives better.
* We have a bias for intentional action — We prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.
* We don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — We are solving an important problem which takes focus, but we also like to enjoy the journey.
* We trust each other and assume good intentions — We're transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

# Data Integrity Officer

## The Role

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Data Integrity Officer to join Cifas and play a key role in maintaining the quality and integrity of our databases. Combining analysis, investigation and attention to detail, the role will review data and emerging trends, respond to consumer complaints in line with data protection legislation, and identify improvements that strengthen the quality and accuracy of information held within our databases.

## Key Responsibilities

Working alongside industry specialists, the successful candidate will be responsible for:

* Providing expert guidance to Cifas members on data processes, delivering a positive member experience and maintaining trust and confidence in Cifas services.
* Reviewing cases and matches to ensure the required standard of proof has been met, results are returned correctly through the relevant delivery channel, and appropriate action is taken to maintain high-quality data.
* Managing and resolving consumer complaints consistently and professionally, working with members where appropriate and representing Cifas in line with our values.
* Managing escalated Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs) and review members’ Fair Processing Notices, ensuring data is handled and filed in accordance with relevant legislation and has an appropriate legal basis.
* Proactively identifying data-quality issues, patterns, anomalies and root causes within Cifas databases, working collaboratively with colleagues and using management information to support effective resolution.
* Recommending improvements to processes and data practices, identifying inefficiencies and clearly demonstrating the value and impact of proposed changes.
* Making informed and considered decisions across cases, complaints, DSARs and Fair Processing Notices, clearly communicating the rationale to members, consumers and other stakeholders within agreed service levels.
* Representing the Data Integrity Officer team at Cifas project and product development meetings, providing subject matter expertise and ensuring Data Integrity Operations considerations are effectively represented.

## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

To be successful in this role, you will have:

* A degree or equivalent level qualification, or relevant professional experience within fraud prevention, financial crime, data integrity or a related environment.
* A strong understanding of fraud prevention, financial crime, the use of Cifas data and relevant Data Protection legislation.
* Detailed knowledge of Cifas Handbooks, systems and how members access and use Cifas data.
* Strong analytical and investigative skills, with excellent attention to detail and the tenacity to identify and resolve complex issues.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence, persuade and appropriately challenge with tact and diplomacy.
* The confidence to take ownership, exercise sound judgement and work collaboratively, while demonstrating integrity, empathy, confidentiality and professionalism.
* The ability to manage competing priorities and deliver to agreed service levels, deadlines and team targets, alongside strong Microsoft 365 skills, particularly Excel, Outlook and Teams.

## Benefits

In return for helping us take the fight to fraud, all our employees receive an impressive benefit package, which includes:

* Remote working with approximately 2 days a month in the London office, although there will be a requirement to attend conventions, forums and events
* Generous annual leave, plus bank holidays
* Private healthcare
* Excellent pension package through salary sacrifice
* Personal and professional growth
* Employee wellbeing – Wellbeing breaks, wellbeing hub access including exercise programmes, meditation guides, sleep stories and yoga.

We have introduced agile ways of working, allowing teams to decide how best they work, while ensuring regular opportunities to collaborate and innovate. We create an environment to help you to unleash your potential and perform the most rewarding work of your career, whilst keeping your wellbeing at the foremost with initiatives in place to promote the wellness of our people.   
   
We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture and have dedicated inclusion champions across the business to celebrate and promote our uniqueness. We also have a dedicated team of volunteers looking for innovative ways to give back as part of our commitments under our Corporate Social Responsibility. Since 2021, we have been recognised in the Best Companies listings, and again in 2026 have been awarded 2 stars for outstanding levels of engagement. We have also been awarded the Investors in People Gold accreditation.  
  
If you are passionate about our purpose and would like an opportunity to make a valuable contribution to fraud prevention, we would like to hear from you.

## About Cifas

Cifas is the UK’s leading fraud prevention service, managing the largest database of instances of fraudulent conduct in the country. Our members are organisations from all sectors, sharing their data across those sectors to reduce instances of fraud and financial crime. Operating as a not-for-profit means our teams put all their efforts into our mission of fighting fraud, rather than creating a financial return for shareholders.

Fraud presents a serious and significant threat to the UK and our role in protecting businesses, the public and the economy from fraud is now more important than ever before. As a result, we have ambitious plans to innovate and create new services and products that will significantly improve the way that we and our members tackle fraud.

Our employees play a crucial part in ensuring we remain the UK's leading fraud prevention service, whilst also ensuring our members remain at the heart of everything we do.

# AI Workflow Transformation Lead

## Job Description

Cint is moving from AI experimentation to enterprise-wide AI-enabled operating change.

The next phase is not about adding more tools or running isolated pilots. It is about helping functions change how work happens: where humans lead, where AI assists, where AI automates, and where autonomous AI can safely operate.

As AI Workflow Transformation Lead, you will work with teams across Cint to identify, shape, deliver and embed AI-enabled improvements. You will help turn business priorities and operational pain points into better workflows, smarter practices and measurable improvements in how work gets done.

This is a broad, hands-on transformation role. Some work may involve workflow redesign. Some may involve functional support, delivery coordination, requirements shaping, governance navigation, adoption support or helping teams move from experiment to scalable practice.

The purpose is simple: help Cint turn AI potential into practical operating improvement.

**Where the role sits**

You will join the AI Transformation Office and report to the Director, Enterprise AI Transformation.

You will work closely with:

* Director, Enterprise AI Transformation — AI roadmap, priorities, governance, value tracking and executive reporting.
* AI Enablement & Adoption Lead — adoption, capability building, manager enablement, playbooks and behaviour change.
* AI/Data Architecture capability — architecture, data readiness, build / buy / configure recommendations and integration design.
* Business Technology — implementation, systems integration and operational handover.
* Legal, DPO, InfoSec, Infrastructure and Functional AI Domain Leads — governance, compliance, technical readiness, business ownership and adoption.

You will not own every system or every team. Your job is to create clarity, momentum and practical progress.

**What you will do**

**Identify and shape opportunities**

You will work with functions to understand their priorities, pain points and opportunities for AI-enabled improvement.

You will help assess where AI can improve speed, quality, productivity, decision-making, risk reduction, employee experience or operating leverage.

You will separate useful opportunities from interesting distractions. Not every AI idea needs a project plan and a parade.

**Redesign work where needed**

You will help teams understand how work happens today and where it gets stuck: manual effort, handoffs, rework, bottlenecks, unclear ownership, data gaps or decision delays.

You will support future-state workflow design before technology is applied.

You will help clarify where work should remain human-led, where AI should assist, where automation makes sense and where review or escalation is needed.

**Support delivery in the right way**

You will help turn AI opportunities into practical plans with clear outcomes, owners, dependencies, risks and success measures.

Depending on the need, you may lead structured transformation work, support a function-led initiative, help shape requirements, coordinate stakeholders, unblock delivery or guide a team through governance.

**Connect business, technical and governance partners**

You will work across functions, AI/Data Architecture, Business Technology, Legal, DPO, InfoSec, Infrastructure and Enablement to make sure AI-enabled improvements are practical, safe and supportable.

You will help ensure the right technical owners, implementation routes, governance gates, adoption plans and handover expectations are clear.

**Measure value and capture learning**

You will define success measures and track whether changes are creating real value.

You will help capture reusable patterns so Cint does not solve the same problem from scratch in every function.

**Support adoption**

You will partner with the AI Enablement & Adoption Lead to make sure new ways of working are understood, adopted and embedded.

You will gather feedback, identify adoption blockers and help teams improve as they go.

## Qualifications

**What we are looking for**

You will likely bring:

* Experience in business transformation, operational excellence, process improvement, programme delivery, consulting, AI transformation, SaaS operations or a similar field.
* Strong ability to understand, map and improve business workflows or operating practices.
* Experience turning ambiguous business problems into clear opportunities, plans and outcomes.
* Comfort working across business, technology, data, automation, legal, risk or compliance stakeholders.
* Practical understanding of AI tools, automation, workflow tooling or digital transformation.
* Good delivery discipline without unnecessary bureaucracy.
* Commercial judgement and a clear link between workflow change and business value.
* Strong communication, facilitation and stakeholder management skills.
* Experience in SaaS, technology, digital platforms, consulting or high-growth global businesses is strongly preferred.

**How you work**

* You are structured, practical and comfortable with ambiguity.
* You are curious about how work really happens, not just how people say it happens.
* You can bring order to messy problems without creating theatre or bureaucracy.
* You influence without authority, communicate clearly and help busy teams make decisions.
* You care about shipped outcomes, measurable value and adoption that sticks.
* You bring low ego, high standards and enough humour to survive cross-functional transformation work.

## Additional Information

**What success looks like**

Within the first 3 months, you will have built a clear understanding of priority functional opportunities, helped shape the first wave of AI-enabled improvement work, and established practical ways of working for opportunity assessment, workflow redesign, delivery support and measurement.

Within 6–9 months, Cint should have visible AI-enabled improvements in priority areas, with clear adoption data, value tracking and reusable learning.

Over time, you will help Cint build a repeatable transformation capability: one that helps functions identify high-value opportunities, redesign work intelligently, apply AI where it makes sense and prove the impact.

## Description

The Senior Executive Protection & Protective Security Advisor is responsible for the planning, coordination and delivery of executive protection and protective security services for senior executives and designated personnel across the UK and Northern Europe.

The role combines strategic risk management with operational delivery, ensuring executives can travel, work and engage globally with confidence. Acting as a trusted security partner to executive offices, regional security teams and external providers, the successful candidate will deliver a discreet, intelligence-led and white-glove protective service while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality and client service.

This position is suited to an experienced corporate security professional with a strong executive protection background, capable of operating confidently within C-suite environments, conducting detailed risk assessments, coordinating complex travel and event security arrangements, and deploying operationally as a Personal Protection Officer (PPO) when required.

## Requirements

## Key Responsibilities

## Executive Protection Operations

* Support the day-to-day delivery of the executive protection programme across the UK and Northern Europe.
* Coordinate protective security activities for senior executives and designated personnel.
* Deploy as a Personal Protection Officer (PPO) when required.
* Maintain oversight of operational tasking, resource allocation and service delivery across all protective activities.
* Ensure all executive protection operations are delivered professionally, discreetly and in accordance with organisational standards.

## Protective Intelligence & Risk Management

* Conduct comprehensive threat, vulnerability and risk assessments for executives, travel, events and strategic business activities.
* Analyse security threats and develop practical mitigation strategies tailored to executive profiles and operational requirements.
* Maintain visibility of executive travel schedules to support proactive threat monitoring and decision-making.
* Monitor geopolitical, criminal, terrorism, civil unrest and emerging security risks impacting executive activities.
* Produce clear, actionable risk assessments and executive security recommendations.

## Travel Security & Journey Management

* Lead advance planning and protective arrangements for domestic and international executive travel.
* Conduct location, venue, accommodation and route risk assessments.
* Develop journey management plans and contingency measures for elevated-risk travel.
* Coordinate security arrangements with regional teams, service providers and local stakeholders.
* Ensure executives receive concise and effective security briefings before travel.

## Event & Residential Security

* Support the design and implementation of security plans for executive meetings, conferences, site visits and corporate events.
* Contribute to residential security reviews and protection programmes for designated personnel.
* Identify vulnerabilities and recommend physical, procedural and technical security enhancements.
* Coordinate security requirements across executive residences, corporate offices and event venues as required.

## Stakeholder Management

* Build trusted relationships with executive offices, senior leadership teams and key business stakeholders.
* Act as a primary point of contact for protective security requirements within the region.
* Coordinate closely with regional security managers, intelligence teams and third-party security providers.
* Ensure all security activities are aligned with corporate policies, governance requirements and risk tolerances.

## Programme Governance & Continuous Improvement

* Maintain accurate records, operational plans and security documentation.
* Support programme reporting, assurance activities and service performance reviews.
* Identify opportunities to enhance executive protection capabilities, processes and standards.
* Contribute to the development of procedures, guidance and best practices for protective services delivery.

## Experience & Qualifications

### Essential

* Minimum 5-8 years' experience within Executive Protection, Protective Services or Corporate Security.
* Demonstrated experience supporting C-suite executives, board members and senior leadership teams.
* Proven experience conducting executive, travel and event security risk assessments.
* Experience planning and coordinating international executive travel and protective operations.
* Strong understanding of threat assessment, protective intelligence and risk mitigation methodologies.
* Experience managing third-party security providers and cross-functional stakeholder relationships.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to brief senior executives confidently.
* Valid driving licence and willingness to travel internationally as operational requirements dictate.

### Desirable

* Previous experience within a multinational corporate environment, global security function, consultancy or professional services organisation.
* Background in specialist military, law enforcement, diplomatic protection or government protective security roles.
* Experience supporting high-profile executive travel in complex or elevated-risk environments.
* Knowledge of crisis management, emergency response and business resilience practices.
* Relevant professional security qualifications and executive protection certifications.

All employees are expected to display behaviours reflective of our company values: Integrity and Ethics, Collaboration and Teamwork, Commitment to People and Professionalism and Excellence.

London, England

# Principal Engineer

Principal Engineer - Contract  
  
About this role  
  
The bar has moved. Five years ago a strong engineer was measured by what they could build and how well they could mentor others to build it. Today, with Claude Code and agents, we produce quality work at a speed that would have looked superhuman in 2022 (Podium, PayPoint, Zuto, RL, OAG Analyser and others).  
  
What separates exceptional from good is no longer typing speed or local craftsmanship. It is the complete package: architecture, deep engineering foundations, communication, system thinking, and the judgement to direct both your own intelligence and AI toward outcomes that matter.   
  
Exceptional people at this level are not the best implementer in the room; they are the person whose specifications, decisions, and review judgement compound into systems that work in production and that others (and agents) can build on. They are a force multiplier, they hold a room at the highest levels, and clients treat them as the SME by default.  
  
Your mindset  
  
The mindset is the engine, and it is almost impossible to teach retrospectively. You are outcome obsessed, not output obsessed and you care whether the problem was actually solved - you resist the ego instinct to admire a clever solution and ask whether it was needed at all.  
  
You are intellectually honest about uncertainty, taking a trust-but-verify approach and assuming the surprising bug is the one that will burn. You are deeply pragmatic, which matters at CreateFuture where pace counts: you have outgrown the religious wars about platforms, languages and patterns, you hold opinions loosely, and you decide for the systems in front of you, not the ones you wish you had.  
  
You have a bias toward delivery: the smallest thing that works, then iterate, treating documents and meetings as means to that end.   
  
And you are relentlessly curious beyond any immediate need, wanting to know how the database actually stores things or why a Claude Opus inference call costs what it does, which keeps you several layers ahead while the rest of the team is still reading the API docs.  
  
AI as the accelerant  
  
For a Principal to be truly exceptional, this is now already a first-class competency in your arsenal, not a side skill. An engineer who is brilliant by last year's standards but not fluent with AI is not exceptional in 2026. In practice that means:

* Setting AI up to succeed. You treat context engineering as a craft (the right files, specs, examples and constraints), and you architect systems with clean interfaces, good naming, machine-readable specs and knowledge bases so the codebase is a quality baseline AI can work on later. No separate ivory-tower architect required.  
  Reviewing and choosing well. You read far more code than you write, and your value is in the quality of review: catching the silent assumption, the security flaw, the architectural drift, knowing where models fail and looking there first. You pick the right tool for the job (Claude Code for a deep refactor, an inline assistant when that is enough, a sub-agent for parallel work, the right model for analysis versus generation) and you know the constraints differ by client, an enterprise like PayPoint or Natwest versus a scale-up type business like Zuto or OAG.  
  Working with non-determinism. You see where AI moves the bottleneck and help people left and right of you unblock the value stream. You build with AI components but know success is no longer a binary, reaching for evals, golden datasets, structured outputs and fallback paths as naturally as you reach for unit tests.

Technical breadth across the full stack  
  
Exceptional means depth in at least one area but competence everywhere the system reaches.

* Backend: an instinct for distributed systems (what fails, what is eventually consistent, where queues back up), APIs that age well, thoughtful data modelling, and an understanding that languages are mostly syntax differences you can close with AI.  
  Cloud: cost-aware and security-aware by default, reaching for IaC, composing the primitives rather than stitching together managed services and hoping it works.  
  Data: modern pipelines, governance and lineage, increasingly vector stores and embeddings, with data quality treated as seriously as production code because garbage in, garbage out is far worse once AI features depend on it.  
  Web and mobile: past the framework arguments, with a clear view on what you would pick today, and able to build "good enough" front ends yourself with AI.

Full-stack here means seeing the platform as one system and knowing which levers matter most. It does not mean front-end work with a few Node.js servers.  
  
System thinking, consulting and commercial judgement  
  
At CreateFuture we work in a consultancy context, where many otherwise excellent IC engineers can struggle.   
  
You know technology is roughly 30% of the picture; the rest is design, argument and reasoning, commercial and political acumen, and the clarity to frame outcomes for a COO, CTO, CIO or CEO in their own language.  
  
You know when gold-plating is wasteful, you can name when a project's real problem is not technical and say so even when it is awkward, and you have a strong sense of what is durable versus what is fashion.   
  
You are not the engineer who introduced the team to seven new technologies last year; you are the one who removed three and quietly made the remaining stack stronger.  
  
Leadership mentality  
  
Technical work is necessary but no longer sufficient. By default you raise the level of everyone around you, regardless of discipline.

* Communicate clearly and frequently (documents, decisions, post-mortems, design notes); the written artefact is the machine-readable context we can feed to AI later.
* Make decisions and own them. You don't escalate everything or hoard control, and you are willing to be the benevolent dictator when it is your turn.
* Mentor in AI fluency, not just code: tooling, prompting and review discipline, so your team is twice as productive a year from now.
* Need little line management. You communicate upwards, raise by exception, self-resolve, and can be trusted with financial controls.
* Disagree well. You tell people they are wrong with evidence and no ego, and you change your own mind when you are shown to be wrong.

What we're not looking for

* The gifted engineer who sits in a silo. This is a team game.
* The one who is fluent with AI but ships without the guardrails and quality gates enterprise clients expect.
* The one with strong technical opinions who cannot justify them commercially and gets defensive when challenged.
* The pure manager who wants to orchestrate teams rather than get involved. This is about setting a new standard, not coordinating it.
* The engineer who will not immerse in a client environment. This role will mean on-site work and trusted relationships built in person. We are not going back to working away from the client and being bypassed.

**About Crunch:**

Crunch is a multi-award winning Software as a Service (SaaS) company, born in the heart of Brighton with a brilliant team of 110, and over 40,000 users of our software.

Crunch isn’t your typical online accountancy firm. We’re a grassroots business built from the ground up, facing the same challenges as our clients. Since 2009, we’ve empowered thousands of small and medium sized businesses to take control of their finances with our simple, effective software, which includes real accountant support. Crunch takes the stress out of accounting, so our clients can focus on doing what they love!

**About the role:**

Accountancy is rarely anyone's idea of glamorous. That's exactly why this role matters.

We need a writer who can make sole traders, contractors and small business owners stop, read and act. In a search result, a news story, an inbox and a text message.

This is a senior role in a sharp, hands-on marketing team, reporting directly to the Director of Marketing. You'll be Crunch's lead writer, owning our articles, our PR and the core messaging in our customer journeys.

Nothing we write is written for the sake of it. Every piece has a reason, a reader and a job to do, whether that's ranking, earning coverage, getting quoted by AI tools or moving someone to sign up. We write to strategy, to outmanoeuvre our competitors and to put Crunch where it needs to be.

**A copywriter first**

You're a copywriter first and foremost. You write for the reader, not just as the brand. You know how to empathise, engage and persuade, and you can make a tax deadline worth reading about. Tools and techniques we can train. The craft and the passion we can't.

**What you'll own**

* SEO articles that rank, get quoted in AI answers and earn their place on our site, planned from our search strategy
* PR. Finding the stories in Crunch, pitching them and getting us covered in the outlets our customers and AI tools read
* Copy for landing pages and advertising
* The core copy and messaging for our email journeys and campaigns, and the texts that go with them. Our CRM & Marketing Automation Specialist builds and sends them, and writes the everyday copy
* Our tone of voice. You'll guard it across everything we publish and sharpen other people's copy
* Quality assurance on our social channels. It's your responsibility, but it's around half a day a month, not the focus of the role
* Knowing what works. Rankings, citations, coverage and the sign-ups your content brings in

**What you'll bring**

* At least 5 years as a professional copywriter or content writer
* Real, hands-on PR experience. You've pitched journalists, landed coverage and know the current tools and techniques for getting a brand noticed
* Solid SEO experience. You know how to research, plan and write content that ranks and gets cited. We'll train you on our tools and take your SEO further
* A real understanding of email journeys. How a sequence builds, what each message has to do and when it should land
* Experience publishing articles through a content management system (CMS)
* Creativity and empathy. You find the human angle in dry subjects
* Commercial sense. You know why you're writing every piece and how it will be judged
* Accuracy. You explain features as benefits without overclaiming, because in finance a wrong figure really matters
* You manage your own time well. You hit your deadlines, and if one's going to slip, you say so early and explain why

**Nice to have**

* Experience in fintech, financial services or SaaS
* Digital PR experience
* An understanding of AEO and GEO, getting content cited in AI answers
* An understanding of FCA rules, UK GDPR and PECR. We can train this
* Using schema for SEO. We can train this too
* Writing scripts for YouTube or video

**Love it or hate it, AI**

We use AI for ideas, research and automation, the things that save us time. We DON’T use it for copy or content, anywhere. Everything that goes out to the public is written by a human.

**How we hire:**

We hire on the strength of your writing. Send us your best work, and we'll talk it through with you at the interview.

**What you’ll get in return:**

We’re very proud of our collaborative and inclusive working environment - you’ll be working as part of a fun and vibrant team, with a whole host of fantastic company benefits!

* Fully remote working in the UK, with no more than a quarterly meet up as required.

* Long service gift awards plus extra holidays for 5, 10 and 15 years’ service.

**The Role**

Every clinical trial depends on a commitment to the people who take part: their rights, safety and wellbeing come first, and the data they help generate can be trusted. Once a product reaches patients, that commitment continues through the monitoring of its safety and benefit-risk. This role holds the organisation to both. As Head of Patient-Facing Quality Assurance, you will lead an integrated QA organisation covering Good Clinical Practice and Good Pharmacovigilance Practice, reporting to the Head of Global R&D Quality. Your team will include PV System and Process Leads, Therapeutic Area Quality Leads, and a Head of Clinical QA or of PV and Regulatory QA, depending on which complements your own background.

  

*Hybrid (3 days a week on site), based in Maidenhead, UK, or King of Prussia, PA, with other global locations open to discussion*

  

**Why it matters**

Bringing clinical and pharmacovigilance quality under one leader is a deliberate choice. Some of the most consequential risks sit at the interfaces between them: serious adverse event reconciliation, expedited reporting, and the safety information that reaches investigators and regulators. A single function can see these clearly and act on them. The role is also a chance to shape how quality is done, not just police it. With ICH E6(R3) moving the industry toward Quality by Design and risk-based quality management, you will set the strategy, operating model and standards for how the company protects participants and patients. You will keep the specialist depth that GCP and GVP each need while making the approach consistent worldwide.

  

**What You’ll Be Responsible For**

You will provide independent, risk-based QA oversight from trial design through close-out, and across the global pharmacovigilance system. You will be the consistent quality voice in governance and a constructive challenger to the functions that own operational delivery.

* Setting the strategy, operating model, governance, capabilities and global resource model for Clinical QA and PV QA, harmonising approaches without diluting specialist expertise
* Embedding Quality by Design, critical-to-quality factors and risk-based quality management, and making sure risks to participant safety, patient safety and data integrity are escalated in time
* Assuring the quality systems behind clinical development and pharmacovigilance, including their integration with the enterprise QMS and accurate representation in the Pharmacovigilance System Master File
* Overseeing the clinical safety interfaces: SAE collection and reconciliation, SUSAR and expedited reporting, investigator safety reporting, safety data exchange agreements and signal escalation
* Running a globally consistent framework for significant quality issues, serious breaches, critical deviations and CAPAs, backed by rigorous root-cause analysis and reportability assessment
* Leading GCP and GVP inspection readiness and health-authority inspections, owning the patient-facing audit plan, and giving senior leadership an integrated view of quality risk, trends and regulatory intelligence

  

**Experience Required**

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in pharma, biotech or regulated life sciences, with a degree in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine, nursing or a related discipline (an advanced degree or professional certification in Quality, GCP, GVP or auditing is an advantage)
* Significant QA leadership in clinical quality, PV quality or both, including leading global teams in a complex matrix; experience across both GCP and GVP is strongly preferred
* Expert knowledge of GCP and GVP regulation and inspection expectations, including ICH E6(R3) and the EU GVP framework
* A track record with health-authority inspections, serious breaches, investigations, CAPAs and inspection remediation
* Hands-on experience of Quality by Design, risk-based quality management, quality metrics, data integrity and computerised systems, as well as oversight of CROs, vendors, affiliates and partners
* Experience managing budgets, consultants, workforce plans and talent, and building a team of trusted strategic advisers

  

**Note on travel**

This is a global role. Expect some out-of-hours meetings across time zones and periodic international travel.

* Support in the recruitment, retention and development of Freedom volunteer foster carers as and when needed.

* Maintain the security architecture and its documentation through life, assessing the security impact of design changes after go-live
