* Validate implementation of security controls against the approved security architecture

* Lead the security architecture contribution to Secure by Design assurance activities

* Working knowledge of UK export controls and, where applicable, ITAR requirements

We're looking for a developer to grow Ember's network of charging hubs. You'll find the sites, take them through legals and planning, manage the build and energise them. How you work and think matters more to us than which industry you've worked in. You think clearly, can run several projects at once and are as at home on a site as behind a desk.
About Ember
We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.
Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.
We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and ~100 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level.
The role
Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline.
You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time.
Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative.
Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs.
It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. Even after a site is live, our involvement doesn't stop. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself.
Diversity and equality
At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.
Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.
What's on offer
You'll receive a salary of £50,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites.
How do I apply?
Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you.
Applications close Friday 27 November at 5pm.


Who we're looking for
You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:
Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one.
Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects.
A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to.
Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote.
Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell.
Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely.
Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet.
A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard.

We are looking for a highly motivated Scientific Developer to join the Chemical Biology Resources team at the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI), located on the Wellcome Genome Campus near Cambridge, UK. This is a 13-month fixed-term position offered as maternity cover. 

The Chemical Biology Resources team provides world-leading chemogenomics resources to the scientific community. ChEMBL is a database of quantitative small-molecule bioactivity data curated primarily from the scientific literature widely used to support drug discovery projects in industry and academia. SureChEMBL is a complementary patent resource containing chemical structures extracted from patents daily. UniChem links chemical structures across databases. ChEBI is a highly curated database and ontology of compounds of biological interest. OPSIN converts systematic chemical names into chemical structures.

The EBI is part of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and it is a world-leading bioinformatics centre providing biological data to the scientific community with expertise in data storage, analysis and representation. EMBL-EBI provides freely available data from life science experiments, performs basic research in computational biology and offers an extensive user training programme, supporting researchers in academic and industry.

Your role

You will develop and maintain software infrastructure to ensure robust, reliable, and automated ChEMBL data releases through streamlined build, packaging, testing, and deployment processes, while also assisting in the development and maintenance of other services supported by the team. You will be working closely with our team which consists of an international and interdisciplinary mix of professional scientists and software engineers.


Main Duties and Responsibilities
Develop and maintain the scientific workflows underpinning the curation, integration and dissemination of the group’s resources (e.g. the data pipelines for generating ChEMBL releases which are a mixture of Python and Java). 
Develop new innovative solutions for enhancing scientific data workflows and support our mission to disseminate scientific information publicly
Manage and enhance scientific software tools essential for processing and storing chemical and biological data across the team’s services, ensuring adherence to software development best practices.
Collaborate with the ChEMBL, SureChEMBL and ChEBI teams to identify and resolve data inconsistencies and quality issues.
Work cross-functionally to integrate computational methodologies into data curation and analysis workflows, including the incorporation of external chemical and bioactivity databases (e.g., BindingDB, PubChem) into the ChEMBL ecosystem.
Support database management, including the maintenance and administration of database instances.
Document workflows and processes to improve maintainability, efficiency, and reproducibility.
Participate in cross functional project meeting with partners on campus (such as Open Targets) and external stakeholders
Contribute to training activities, and participate in scientific meetings

You have:
A PhD or equivalent experience in Chemistry, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Data Science, or a related field.
Experience in cheminformatics or data engineering applied to life sciences
Proficiency in Python, with experience in cheminformatics libraries and topics (such as RDKit, Open Babel, InChI, SMILES/SMARTS)
Experience working with relational (SQL) databases
Familiarity working in a structured collaborative data and software development environment (git, GitHub/GitLab)
Proficient in working with Linux operating systems.
Self-motivated with good communication skills and the ambition to work with international collaborators and users. 
Can-do attitude and willingness to help solve problems
Advanced English language and excellent interpersonal skills

You might have:
Familiarity with containerization technologies (Docker)
Basic understanding of Java, with a willingness to develop expertise and contribute to Java-based pipelines as needed

We are seeking a Technical Product Owner to help shape the next generation of Eque2’s cloud estimating and cost-control software. Reporting to the Chalkstring Product Director, you will own backlog quality, prioritisation and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management, defining clear requirements and testable acceptance criteria for Engineering and QA.

You will partner with Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA from discovery and rapid prototyping through to customer delivery and validation. You will use AI-enabled product, design and development tools to accelerate this process and play a central role in expanding Chalkstring with capabilities from our established EValuate product.

You will engage directly with customers to understand their processes, validate use cases, explore emerging AI opportunities and support acceptance testing, using customer and delivery evidence to inform product decisions.

**Location:** This is a UK-based hybrid role, with office access in Maidenhead and Newcastle-upon-Tyne. Travel is required for team, customer and stakeholder meetings, with office attendance expected 1–2 days per week.

**Is this role right for you?**

This is a hands-on product delivery role rather than a Product Management position.

You will have authority over the delivery backlog, priorities and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management. Product Management retains ownership of overall product strategy, roadmap direction, pricing and market positioning.

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to customers, Engineering and delivery, and who can turn broad product direction and complex customer needs into well-defined work that teams can confidently build and test.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and prioritise the delivery backlog within Product Management’s agreed direction, making trade-offs, dependencies and delivery decisions visible.
* Turn validated customer needs into delivery-ready epics, stories, workflows and acceptance criteria that Engineering and QA can implement and test without repeated clarification.
* Lead refinement and contribute actively to sprint planning and reviews, resolving ambiguity quickly and accepting completed work against agreed criteria.
* Engage directly with construction customers to understand estimating and cost-control workflows, validate use cases and edge cases, and support user acceptance and adoption.
* Use AI-enabled development, design and product management tools to accelerate research, requirements, prototyping and delivery while maintaining appropriate review, security and data controls.
* Identify and validate valuable customer-facing AI opportunities, defining quality thresholds, safeguards, human oversight and evaluation requirements for probabilistic features.
* Work closely with Product Design, Engineering and QA on workflows, data models, integrations, APIs, technical constraints and testability.
* Measure adoption, quality and customer outcomes; use evidence to guide iteration, priorities and recommendations to Product Management.
* Communicate progress, decisions, risks and dependencies clearly, and keep product documentation, release notes, Support and Customer Success briefings current.

**Knowledge, Skills & Experience**

* Demonstrable experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst or in a closely related B2B SaaS delivery role.
* Practical experience owning and prioritising backlogs within an Agile delivery environment.
* A strong track record of translating customer and operational needs into clear user stories, requirements and testable acceptance criteria.
* Strong process, workflow and data analysis skills.
* Enough technical understanding to discuss APIs, integrations, data and dependencies confidently with Engineering teams.
* Hands-on experience using AI tools in areas such as product discovery, analysis, design, requirements or prototyping.
* An understanding of the quality, risk and human-oversight considerations associated with customer-facing AI.
* Confidence engaging directly with customers and communicating technical and product decisions to different audiences.
* An evidence-led, proactive and collaborative approach, with strong attention to detail.
* Experience using Jira or a comparable product delivery tool.

**Desirable**

* Construction estimating, quantity surveying or cost control.
* EValuate or other construction estimating software.
* AI, machine-learning or data-driven product capabilities within complex B2B workflows.
* AI prototyping, evaluation or observability tools.
* Low-code or no-code platforms or AI coding assistants.
* SQL.
* API tools such as Postman or Swagger.
* Process modelling, including BPMN.

**Personal attributes**

You are a practical, customer-focused Product Owner who enjoys turning complex operational problems into clear, deliverable outcomes.

You are comfortable getting into the detail with engineers while keeping sight of the customer problem and intended outcome. You ask precise questions, challenge assumptions and identify dependencies early rather than allowing ambiguity to reach Engineering.

You will be:

* **Curious and evidence-led**, using customer and delivery insight to inform decisions.
* **Proactive and solutions-focused**, comfortable resolving ambiguity and moving work forward.
* **Commercially and technically credible**, able to communicate confidently with customers, engineers and senior stakeholders.
* **Collaborative and adaptable**, working effectively across Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA.
* **Quality-conscious**, balancing pace and innovation with security, responsible AI use and customer trust.

**The successful candidate will be:**

* Highly organised, detail-oriented and effective at managing time and priorities.
* Professional, credible and confident when engaging with senior stakeholders.
* Proactive, solutions-focused and able to anticipate needs.
* Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities.
* Trustworthy, discreet and demonstrates sound judgement.
* Collaborative, approachable and service oriented.
* A positive ambassador for the organisation’s culture, values and standards.

**Measures of Success**

**Success in this role will be demonstrated through:**

* **Backlog readiness:** priority work has a clear outcome, scope, acceptance criteria and dependencies before it reaches sprint planning.
* **Requirement quality:** Engineering and QA can implement and test work without recurring clarification, with requirement-related rework reduced over time.
* **Delivery predictability:** risks, dependencies and material scope changes are identified and communicated early.
* **Customer validation:** priority features are tested with representative customers and validated against defined needs and use cases.
* **AI quality and safety:** customer-facing AI capabilities meet agreed standards for quality, reliability, privacy, security and appropriate human oversight before release.
* **Adoption and value:** released capabilities have clear outcome measures, such as adoption, usage, satisfaction or operational improvement, which are reviewed after launch.
* **AI-enabled productivity:** AI tools demonstrably improve discovery, prototyping or delivery without weakening quality, controls or traceability.
* **Operational readiness:** relevant documentation, release notes and Support and Customer Success briefings are complete before launch.

# The FT World Desk Fellowship

United Kingdom

**About us**

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*

**Our commitment to inclusion and fairness**

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

**The Financial Times has an exciting opportunity for aspiring Black foreign correspondents.**

Are you keen to report on the world at this time of tumult? Are you excited by international news and do you want a hand in interpreting and explaining it to a global audience? Are you tempted by the idea of a wide-ranging career in journalism reporting on dramatic events from across the globe? If so, then our new six-month World Desk fellowship would suit you well.   

The FT’s global, award-winning editorial team represents the gold standard in journalism, seeking depth, originality and balance that differentiates the FT from the pack and engages subscribers.

The Fellowship is a six-month, paid fellowship in the heart of the FT’s London newsroom. You will join the World News Desk, where a dozen-strong team of accomplished journalists commission and edit our global coverage.   

You will work with the editors to help deliver ground-breaking coverage. You will also work closely with our London-based regional editors, the Africa Editor, Europe Editor, Latin America Editor and Middle East Editor, helping them with their coverage.

You will support the global network of correspondents with research and ideas for how to complement their stories with the right data and visual elements. You will be encouraged to write your own stories and will have mentoring from senior FT editors, in particular the foreign editor, in how to conceive and craft an “FT story”.

**What You Will Learn**

You will be part of a team of experienced journalists covering the world, and there may also be opportunities for short-term stints on other editorial desks. You will learn the timeless arts of writing clear crisp copy and reporting on complex and sensitive stories. 

You will also gain insight into the essential skills of cutting-edge digital journalism and story-telling. The overarching ambition of the fellowship is to help to equip you one day to be a foreign correspondent, hopefully for the FT.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

The successful candidate will:

* Display a keen interest in international affairs
* Want to pursue a career in journalism covering global news
* Be capable of keeping a cool head under deadline pressure
* Care deeply about writing accurately and objectively

Some experience in journalism is preferable but not essential. Career change applications are also welcome.

This opportunity is designed for Black candidates to help to address historical under-representation in the media, and to support greater diversity.

**How to apply**

All applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom.

Please upload **three documents**:

* **CV**
* **A Cover Letter detailing what you will bring to the role and why you think you are suitable**
* **An unpublished article on an international story (600 words max)**

The deadline for applications is 8pm on Sunday 15th November 2026.

**Further information**

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and to take a short writing test. The successful applicant will join the World News Desk and report to the FT’s Foreign Editor, Alec Russell.  

This 6-month fellowship is for 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, starting in Spring 2027.

The fellow will receive a monthly bursary of £2,500.

**The use of AI**

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism.  Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

**Accessibility**

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

# Events and Campaigns Manager

## **A bit about us**

GEEIQ helps brands and agencies understand, plan and measure their activity across gaming and virtual worlds. We combine platform data with specialist expertise to help marketing teams make informed decisions about where to invest and how to measure success.

In 2027 we launch a new product for brand and agency media teams. Events and campaigns are how we bring it to market.

## **The role**

We are looking for an Events and Campaigns Manager to own the delivery of GEEIQ's events and marketing campaigns.

Events come first. You will plan and run our own buyer events, manage our presence at industry events, and build the campaigns that surround them: the invitation programme with Sales, the build-up, the event itself and the follow-up. Alongside this, you will deliver ongoing campaigns promoting GEEIQ's content, expertise and services.

Your immediate priority will be the launch of a new GEEIQ product in spring 2027. This includes the pre-launch programme, buyer events in London and Los Angeles, and our presence at SXSW in March and MadFest in July.

Marketing at GEEIQ is a small team. You will work directly with our marketing lead, who owns strategy, positioning and content, with support on audience lists, campaign operations and reporting. Your job is to turn those inputs into events and campaigns that run well, making the day-to-day delivery decisions yourself.

## **What success looks like**

Events and campaigns are delivered to agreed timelines and budgets. Guests are invited, tracked and followed up. Colleagues and suppliers understand their responsibilities, materials are ready when needed, and problems are raised early enough to resolve.

Sales receives timely, useful follow-up information. Reporting informs the next round of activity. Clear ownership and dependable execution give the rest of the team more time for strategy, content and customer conversations.

## Key Responsibilities

### **Plan and deliver events**

* Own event planning and logistics from the initial brief through to event-day delivery and post-event follow-up: venues, quotes, bookings, registration, guest communications, materials and running orders.
* Run the invitation programme for each event with Sales: agree invite targets per person, track invitations through to registration and attendance, and report progress weekly.
* Deliver our own buyer events in London and Los Angeles, and organise GEEIQ's participation in agreed industry events, including preparation, meeting coordination and supporting communications.
* Find and secure speaking opportunities for our founders at events where media buyers gather, and prepare the briefing and follow-up around them.
* Coordinate speakers, suppliers and internal contributors so that everyone understands their responsibilities.

### **Own campaign delivery**

* Turn approved briefs into delivery plans with clear milestones, responsibilities, budgets and measures of success, and maintain the campaign calendar.
* Coordinate email, social, website and other agreed activity, working with marketing operations and specialist suppliers where needed.
* Write event invitations, reminders, promotional emails, short social posts and follow-up communications using approved messaging, and adapt reports, articles and case studies into campaign materials suited to each audience and channel.
* Manage asset requirements, production schedules and approval deadlines, checking that materials are accurate, on brand and ready to use.
* Identify competing deadlines and capacity constraints early, and recommend practical changes to keep priority activity on track.

### **Manage suppliers and budgets**

* Brief suppliers clearly, assess work against agreed requirements and manage deadlines.
* Track committed costs and actual spend, keeping an accurate view of each campaign or event budget.
* Make routine delivery decisions within agreed limits, seek approval for material changes to scope, cost or messaging, and build reusable briefs, schedules and checklists that make future delivery more efficient.

### **Connect activity with follow-up and results**

* Agree follow-up responsibilities and timing with Sales before events and campaigns go live, and provide clear handovers with the relevant audience, engagement and event context.
* Bring together reporting on response, registrations, attendance, follow-up and spend, supported by marketing operations.
* Review results, gather feedback and recommend improvements to future delivery.

## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

### **What you need to succeed**

* Experience delivering business events and B2B marketing campaigns from planning through to follow-up.
* Confidence handling event logistics and resolving practical problems on the day.
* Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage several deadlines, suppliers and internal contributors at once.
* Clear, accurate writing, with the ability to adapt existing messages into effective campaign communications.
* Experience working within agreed budgets, reviewing quotes and tracking costs.
* Familiarity with CRM and marketing tools, and confidence using campaign reporting.
* An understanding of how marketing activity supports conversations with prospective customers.
* The judgement to act independently within an agreed brief and recognise when a decision needs wider input.

### **Nice to have**

* Experience running invitation-led events for senior audiences, in the UK and the US.
* Experience working with brand marketers, agency teams or paid media buyers.
* Experience in B2B technology, SaaS, media or advertising.
* Familiarity with HubSpot.
* Experience coordinating product launches.
* An interest in gaming and virtual worlds.

Gaming expertise is not essential. We are looking for someone who can understand the audience, organise the work and deliver it reliably.

## About GEEIQ

Go Virtual with GEEIQ - we’re the data platform helping brands like Walmart, Gucci, L’Oréal and Porsche navigate, measure and grow across virtual worlds. Think Ralph Lauren in Fortnite or Elton John in Roblox, that’s where we come in.

Based in London, our 40-person team combines platform data and human expertise to help the world’s biggest brands navigate this new marketing frontier. We believe the metaverse hype is over; brands now demand measurement, attribution and real ROI. That’s what we deliver.

Every idea is valued here - we’re collaborative, curious and ambitious, shaping how brands Go Virtual with confidence.

## About Gradiated

1. Gradiated is a research lab focused on inference. We co-design software and hardware for efficiently serving open-weight models.
2. Our goal is to maximize intelligence per joule. We work across model behavior, software, systems, and silicon to find better ways to run models.
3. We start by thinking about the model as a mathematical function, and map that out onto hardware and then build software on top of that which is custom to each model. This maximises performance and removes wasted abstractions.
4. We are early. You will help set the technical direction and the way the company works.

## Why this role exists

1. We are building an inference research team to find where current hardware and software waste time, memory, and energy when serving open-weight models.
2. You will measure those bottlenecks, test changes across the inference stack, and turn useful results into production systems. Your findings will also inform our silicon work.

## What you will do

1. Measure target models and workloads on current NVIDIA and AMD hardware.
2. Design and implement kernels, numerical formats, memory layouts, and cache policies.
3. Change runtimes, schedulers, distributed execution, and serving paths when they limit the system.
4. Test latency, throughput, energy use, model quality, correctness, and reliability on real workloads.
5. Turn research results into production services.
6. Share research publicly so that others can learn about how inference research is done.
7. Work with the silicon team to identify hardware bottlenecks and design opportunities.

## Problems you may work on

1. Kernels and fused execution paths for exact model shapes.
2. Low-bit formats that preserve model quality.
3. KV-cache layout, movement, compression, and reuse.
4. Sparse and mixture-of-experts execution.
5. Speculative and parallel decoding.
6. Prefill and decode scheduling across multiple GPUs.
7. Performance models that explain the gap between hardware limits and measured results.
8. Runtime designs for long-running agent workloads.

## What we are looking for

1. You have built an ML systems, compiler, runtime, or kernel project, and you can explain your decisions and results in detail.
2. You can work in Python and a systems language such as C++ or Rust. We use C++ mostly.
3. You can write CUDA or HIP kernels, or you have strong low-level systems experience and can learn GPU programming.
4. You understand transformer execution, including attention, memory movement, and numerical precision.
5. You use profiling and controlled experiments to identify system limits.
6. You are open to learning about hardware, and what is limiting the execution of the model.
7. You can maintain production code, not only experimental code.
8. You can explain hard technical solutions clearly

## This role is not for you if

1. You want to work within one layer of the inference stack.
2. You want framework integration to be the main technical work.
3. You want papers or notebook results to be the primary output.
4. You aren't excited by rewriting things from scratch, and taking time to find the globally optimal solution to a problem.
5. You need a complete specification before you can investigate a problem.

## How we work

1. We like to experiment a lot and do the hard thing even if it's likely to fail.
2. We work in the office on Monday, Wednesday, Friday. We value working in person to solve hard problems, but are also flexible, some of the team work abroad for short periods.

## Pay and equity

1. We offer top-of-market compensation, with significant equity.
2. We pay at the top of the market because talent density is what allows us to build the most efficient inference. We want a small team of exceptional people who have fun solving hard problems together.

## Interview process

1. 01A 60-minute call about your goals and the role.
2. 02We get together in person and talk through the problems we will work on.
3. 03A paid in-person working session, so we can get to know you and you can meet the team.
4. 04References and an offer decision.

GSK’s Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be embedded in a team shaping how AI transforms GSK’s process development around the world. This role will build Physical AI capabilities to create self-driving labs and simulated tech transfers. You will work on orchestration of the physical space from the digital space. As our Senior Product Manager you’ll own a new suite of AI and ML-powered data products at the forefront of innovation in the market research industry. 👉 Shaping our approach to responsible AI, covering transparency, data governance, privacy and explainability, so clients can trust what the products tell them

👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, market and competitor insight, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, then prioritising the most valuable work

👉 Taking products from early discovery and prototyping through to launch and adoption, including shaping the commercial model, pricing and packaging with Finance and Revenue teams (including usage-based and consumption models)

👉 Communicating progress, trade-offs and results clearly to the Exec team and wider business

👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn’t complete, and you’re happy taking a big initiative and running with it

👉 You’re a strong problem solver, negotiator, and influencer. You get alignment without needing authority

👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers

👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering, data science and design solutions

👉 Bonus points if you’ve worked in market research, consumer insight or analytics, with large-scale survey or behavioural datasets, or on usage-based pricing for AI or API products

It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.

*The Enterprise Transformation Programme is a multi-year journey focused on transforming the Haleon business building an organisation that is wired for excellence to be able to deliver our ‘Win as One’ strategy and drive growth through continuous improvement. The programme aims to strengthen the heartbeat of our business enabling us to become more agile, efficient, and innovative and is enabled through SAP S/4HANA. The Business Process Expert partners with Business Process Owners and functional teams to design, govern, and continuously improve end-to-end business processes.*

  

**Role purpose** 

The Supply Planning BPE is responsible for shaping, measuring and continuously improving Supply Planning process elements within the P2F (Plan-to-Forecast) value stream to deliver business value (service, cost, inventory and agility). The role partners with the P2F Business Process Owner (BPO) and other BPEs to manage the current process (including ensuring proposed changes are aligned to the intended future state), define the future end‐to‐end process vision and roadmap, ensure high‐quality, well‐controlled and user‐centric processes are created, and drive the transition from current state to future state through disciplined execution, strong governance and effective change delivery. 

  

A key focus of this role is enabling SAP S/4HANA capabilities relating to Supply Planning and ensuring effective integration of IBP outputs into Production Planning to support execution. The BPE supports the BPO in maximising value delivery through rigorous performance management, adoption oversight and continuous improvement activities, ensuring committed benefits are realised and sustained.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**1) Process design, planning and coordination (Supply Planning in P2F)**

* Collaborate with the BPO and relevant functions (e.g. CoE, Sites, CMOs, Planning Hubs) / Operating Units to ensure Supply Planning process design meets requirements and strategic objectives across planning horizons (strategic, RCCP, tactical, and operational execution).

* Facilitate workshops to gather input, feedback, and socialise recommendations with functions/operating units to refine and finalise process design in partnership with the BPO and other BPEs.

* Collaborate with the BPO to document “to be” processes; and support evaluation of “as is” processes identifying bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and duplication.

* Define how Supply Planning connects end-to-end, including:

* Translation of plans across horizons (strategic capacity views → RCCP → tactical supply plans → short-term execution)

* Integration points between IBP outputs (e.g., agreed supply plan, constraints, scenarios, priorities) and Production Planning & Detailed Scheduling for execution (e.g., planning parameters, MRP/MPS triggers, production proposals, exception handling).

* Ensure the process provides clear visibility of product lifecycle from NPI through maturity to phase-out and obsolescence, including governance for phase-in/phase-out and inventory risk management.

* Drive decisions through relevant governance forums, ensuring decisions are communicated to stakeholders in a timely manner.

* Align designs with programme timelines and milestones, ensuring coordination with other functional areas and interdependent programmes (including data, tooling, master data, and site/market deployment waves).

  

**2) Readiness for delivery (including S/4HANA enablement)** 

* Support the BPO and Functional Leaders in evaluating preparedness of their functional area for programme delivery, identifying any gaps and proposing solutions.

* Support the business change team in understanding people implications for the change and defining and delivering relevant interventions to create conditions for successful adoption.

* Create appropriate documentation for new processes; partnering with Training & Adoption team to develop role-based training/upskilling for planners and execution teams to support adoption and benefit realisation.

* Support process and business readiness specifically for S/4HANA-enabled Supply Planning and execution, including:

* Process alignment to S/4HANA planning and execution capabilities (and required ways of working)

* Definition of required master data/process controls to ensure stable planning outputs (e.g., lead times, lot sizes, BOM/routings readiness, production versions, planning calendars, MRP parameters—where applicable)

* Clear operational procedures for exceptions, rescheduling, constraint management and escalation from S/4 execution signals back into the planning cycle.

  

**3) Supporting planning & execution of NPI (New Product Introduction)** 

* Ensure Supply Planning processes support NPI planning and execution end-to-end (from first forecast and supply readiness through ramp-up and stabilisation).

* Partner with I2M BPO and cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., category/brand, R&D, Quality, Regulatory, Procurement, Manufacturing, Customer Service) to embed NPI governance into planning, including:

* Planning assumptions, scenario planning, capacity/material readiness and pre-build strategies

* Cutover planning for launch, allocation/prioritisation rules where constrained, and service risk mitigation

* Ensure robust lifecycle controls for phase-in/phase-out, including inventory run-down, substitution rules, and obsolescence management aligned to governance.

  

**4) Managing transition phases** 

* Partner with the Business Continuity Manager to establish and manage interim operating states to support business continuity during the change (including system/process cutovers).

* Collaborate with operational teams to design and implement interim processes, ensuring minimal disruption to existing operations.

* Ensure that plans are in place to transition from interim states to permanent processes in a sustainable way (including hypercare, stabilisation criteria, and handover to BAU ownership).

  

**5) Performance management and continuous improvement** 

* Support the BPO in defining, tracking and improving Supply Planning performance, including measures that connect plan quality to execution outcomes (e.g., service, schedule adherence, stability, inventory health, exception volumes and resolution time).

* Use data-driven insights to identify root causes of planning/execution gaps (e.g., plan-to-produce mismatch, parameter issues, master data quality, constraint visibility) and drive sustainable improvements.

* Ensure continuous improvement activities are prioritised against business value and embedded into standard routines.

  

**6) Stakeholder engagement** 

* Foster effective relationships with stakeholders across planning and execution, ensuring alignment and collaboration.

* Communicate effectively, adapting messaging for different audiences to ensure clarity and engagement in programme objectives.

* Champion the process vision, ensuring priorities are reflected in programme decision-making and feedback loops are effective.

 

**Qualifications**

* Experience working in complex, global organisations, ideally within Consumer Health or FMCG sectors.

* Strong analytical skills; ability to analyse complex planning and execution processes, understand workflow patterns, and identify inefficiencies.

* Strong understanding of Supply Planning concepts across planning horizons (strategic, RCCP, tactical, operational execution) and how decisions translate into manufacturing and supply execution.

* Experience enabling ERP-based planning/execution, with strong preference for SAP S/4HANA exposure; ability to translate business requirements into system-enabled process design and controls.

* Understanding of how IBP outputs (plans, scenarios, constraints, prioritisation) should integrate into S/4HANA Production Planning processes to drive executable plans.

* Experience supporting NPI planning and launch execution, including lifecycle management through to phase-out/obsolescence.

* Knowledge of process modelling software, data analysis tools, and familiarity with automation technologies is beneficial.

* Project management skills: ability to plan, manage, and execute process improvement initiatives.

* Inspiring and motivating – strong leader who can energise teams toward shared goals.

* Building strong relationships – skilled at developing collaborative connections across functions.

* Making informed decisions – evaluates challenges from multiple perspectives, analyses outcomes, takes calculated risks, and drives timely decisions.

* Navigating and driving change – applies structured change management strategies, guides teams through uncertainty, and maintains operational stability and continuity throughout transformation.

As a global digital-native FMCG company and the world's leading mealkit provider, we are transforming the traditional food supply chain through a data-driven, on-demand model that enables scalable and more sustainable food delivery. The Planning team is the most data-driven team at HelloFresh: we plan, schedule and analyse the production of every box before it reaches our hungry customers across the UK. * **Production & Capacity Planning:** Build and maintain accurate production plans based on forecast demand, operational capacity, production constraints and site requirements.

* **Plan vs Actual Analysis:** Analyse planned versus actual performance, identify deviations and investigate the underlying drivers rather than simply reporting the variance.
* **Operational Problem Solving:** Use data to identify constraints, test assumptions and develop practical solutions to complex production and planning problems.
* **Continuous Improvement & Automation:** Identify opportunities to simplify, automate and improve planning processes, including the practical application of AI and analytical tools.
* **Stakeholder Partnership:** Work closely with Operations and cross-functional teams to understand requirements, challenge assumptions and ensure plans are executable on the production floor.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

## **About the Role**

The engineering intern position is for an individual contributor who is responsible for architecting, implementing, and maintaining significant systems that serve hundreds of millions of requests per month. Hiya provides high-availability, latency-sensitive capabilities to telecoms, mobile apps, and other partners. In addition, you'll work with engineering teams across Hiya, some in Seattle and some in Europe, to define and deliver shared components and services. From day one, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who provides structured guidance, technical feedback, and ongoing career mentorship.

## **What You'll Do**

Design, code, and operate high-performance services and data processing pipelines on a modern technology stack, supported by a structured technical crash course during your first two weeks covering our core tools, architecture, and repositories.

Work at a supportive and fast-growing startup with a fantastic team, where you can collaborate with and learn from other great team members.

Make an impact in the lives of hundreds of millions of consumers.

Be supported in developing your skills and accelerating your career.

## **What We Are Looking For**

* **Engineering:** CS majors - 2nd year (graduating 2028)
* Excitement to work on innovative technology advancements
* A philosophy of iteration and continuous improvement
* Working knowledge of building services that adhere to operational SLAs
* A preference for velocity over perfection
* A commitment to respectful and impactful collaboration
* Self-motivated and excited to learn about new technologies

## **Our Interview Process: The Hiya Voice AI Challenge**

Once we’ve confirmed your eligibility, you’ll receive the Hiya Voice AI Challenge by email-- a chance to build a working prototype of a voice-driven product in one of five tracks: Accessibility, Productivity, Creative Voice, Security, or Real-Time Assistance. You’ll have one week to build it, with optional virtual office hours along the way if you’d like to pitch your idea and get steering from our team first.

From there:

* **Submit and get reviewed.** One of our engineers reviews your work. If we’d like to explore your project further, you’ll get a link to book a 30-minute virtual session with an engineer or two-- a quick demo, a walkthrough of your code, and some questions.
* **Final interviews, in person at Hiya.** Candidates who advance join us for a final round in London (**2nd & 3rd of December)**: a debugging/fixing session, a chance to add a feature to your own project, and a conversation about Hiya’s values.

AI tools are welcome and encouraged the whole way through.

## **What You Can Expect From Us**

* Dedicated technical mentorship with structured, regular feedback check-ins
* Clear project scope and goals provided right at the start of your internship
* Comprehensive onboarding to get you up to speed on Hiya's tooling, codebases, and systems quickly
* A supportive, collaborative environment built on psychological safety and genuine impact

## **How We Work**

Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems.

We work with a high degree of **transparency and autonomy**. Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward.

You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust.

Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values:

* Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality
* Own, share in success and open up to failures
* Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made
* Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves
* Do, rather than observe

We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career.

We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us!

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

# **About the Engineering team**

At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology.

Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users.

## **About the role**

Underwriters at the world's largest insurers still do much of their work in spreadsheets, email threads, and systems that were never designed for the decisions they are making. We are rebuilding that from the ground up.

You will join the Workflow Underwriting stream, building the next generation of our underwriting platform. This is not a platform with AI features bolted on. We are designing it around the agents we build, which means the architecture, the domain model, and the interaction patterns are all genuinely open questions. You will help answer them.

You will contribute at code, architecture, and domain level from your first weeks, and you will talk directly to the underwriters who use what you build.

## **What you’ll be doing**

* Design, build, and operate backend services in Kotlin or Java, and own them in production.
* Turn ambiguous underwriting problems into simple, reliable software. Much of the work is deciding what to build, not just building it.
* Shape architectural decisions: APIs, domain models, persistence, reliability, observability, and how the platform evolves without collapsing under its own weight.
* Build real depth in the underwriting domain, to the point where you can challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.
* Design and build agent-assisted workflows, and make judgement calls about where an agent should act, where it should advise, and where a human must stay in control.
* Use AI coding tools, including Claude, as a core part of how you work. You delegate substantial work to them and you remain accountable for the quality, security, and correctness of everything you ship.
* Work across boundaries with frontend engineers, product partners, and client-facing teams, and step outside your specialism when the problem demands it.
* Give and take direct feedback, and raise the engineering bar around you.

## **What you’ll need to have done**

* Strong professional experience building and running backend systems in Kotlin, Java, or another JVM language.
* Judgement in architecture and system design: a feel for what to build now, what to defer, and what will hurt in two years.
* Evidence of shipping software that solved a real customer or business problem, ideally something you owned end to end.
* A self-starting approach. You find the highest-value problem rather than waiting for a ticket.
* Clear communication. You can hold the same conversation with an underwriter, an executive, and an engineer, and adjust for each.
* Genuine appetite for problems with no known answer, and comfort working without a precedent to copy.
* Confident, responsible use of AI coding tools, with a critical eye on their output.
* Receptiveness to feedback. We give it directly and often, and we expect you to give it back.

## **Helpful, not required**

* Experience in insurance, underwriting, or another complex regulated domain. We will teach you the domain. We cannot teach curiosity about it.
* Experience across both backend and frontend.
* Experience building workflow, decision-support, or agent-assisted products.
* Experience working directly with enterprise clients.

## **You’re unlikely to thrive here if**

* You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.
* You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.
* You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our **Culture Document** leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

## **Compensation**

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

**Equity:** We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this.

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

**About Intercontinental Exchange**

Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE:ICE) is a Fortune 500 company operating a leading network of global futures, equity, and equity options exchanges, alongside world-class clearing and data services spanning financial and commodity markets.

We place the needs of our customers and global market participants at the forefront of everything we do. As a high-growth organisation, we pioneered transparency and risk management in global derivatives markets. Our team comprises engineers, strategists, and problem-solvers who continuously innovate technology solutions to address complex market structure challenges.

The ICE Data Derivatives business provides market data, valuation, and analytics services across all OTC derivative asset classes to a global customer base.

We are looking for a Financial Engineer to join the team that builds and maintains the volatility models and exotic pricers used by our clients, including front-office trading desks that rely on our solution to risk-manage their exotics books every day.

You will work on two core areas: fitting implied volatility smiles across Equity and FX and improving the accuracy and stability of our equity and FX exotics pricers and their risks. You will also apply modern AI and machine learning techniques to speed up risk computation.

Your work will directly affect the prices, Greeks and risk numbers that traders and risk managers act on, so precision, robustness and clear communication matter as much as technical depth.

**Responsibilities**

Volatility Modelling and Smile Calibration

* Build, improve and maintain analytical and semi-analytical models to fit option smile and surface data across Equity and FX.
* Ensure calibrated surfaces are arbitrage-free, stable over time and robust to noisy or sparse market data.
* Handle asset-class specifics: dividends and borrow for equity, delta and quote conventions for FX.

Exotics Pricing and Risk

* Enhance pricing models and numerical methods (Monte Carlo, PDE, semi-analytical) for equity and FX exotics such as barriers, autocallables, cliquets, basket and worst-of products.
* Improve the accuracy and stability of prices and sensitivities, including smooth Greeks, convergence, handling of discontinuities and consistency between pricing and risk.
* Investigate and resolve pricing and risk issues raised by traders, risk managers and clients, and explain model behaviour in practical terms.
* Contribute to model validation, back-testing and benchmarking.

Next-Generation Risk Analytics

* Leverage advanced AI techniques (e.g. neural-network pricers and calibrators, surrogate models, algorithmic differentiation, Chebyshev or regression-based approximations) to significantly accelerate Value-at-Risk (VaR) and XVA computations.
* Assess the accuracy, stability and limitations of accelerated methods against reference pricers, in particular for risk and hedging use.

AI-Accelerated Development

* Use AI coding tools to speed up the development, testing, refactoring and documentation of pricing and calibration code, and share effective practices with the team.
* Validate AI-generated code rigorously (unit tests, convergence checks, comparison against reference implementations, code review), so that faster delivery does not compromise numerical accuracy or model governance.

Research and Documentation

* Produce rigorous analysis and comprehensive documentation of model methodologies, architectures and research findings to support transparency, model governance and knowledge transfer across the organisation.

Large-Scale Data Analysis

* Extract insights from complex, high-volume market and risk datasets to inform model development, diagnose model behaviour and shape business strategy.

Model Interpretation and Client Guidance

* Provide clear explanations of model behaviour (including AI-based models), conduct scenario analysis and deliver actionable analytics to stakeholders such as front-office traders, risk managers, sales and technology teams.

**Knowledge and Experience**

* Proven experience as a quant in derivatives pricing or modelling at a bank, hedge fund, vendor or consultancy.
* Strong knowledge of option pricing theory, stochastic calculus and volatility modelling (local vol, stochastic vol, local-stochastic vol, smile dynamics).
* Hands-on experience calibrating volatility surfaces and building or validating exotic option pricers in equity and/or FX.
* Solid grasp of numerical methods: Monte Carlo, finite-difference/PDE, optimisation and interpolation.
* Strong programming skills in Python and C++ (or a comparable compiled language), with good software engineering practices (testing, version control, code review).
* Proficiency with AI coding assistants and agentic tools (e.g. Claude, Codex, Copilot), with a track record of using them to deliver code, research and documentation significantly faster, while keeping the rigour expected of production quant libraries.
* Ability to communicate complex quantitative topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
* Master’s or PhD in Mathematics, Physics, Financial Engineering, Computer Science or a related quantitative field.

**Core Competencies**

* Rigour and attention to detail, with a focus on numerical stability and risk accuracy.
* Curiosity and willingness to explore new techniques while understanding their limits.
* Ownership of problems from diagnosis through to production delivery.
* A collaborative approach and the ability to work with traders, risk managers and developers.

# Technical Author

Evesham, GBR

Business Unit: Matcon

Join IDEX Material Processing Technologies and be part of a team that provides specialist equipment & solutions for powder material handling & blending, particle size reduction, and liquid processing for the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food, and biopharmaceutical sectors. Here, you’ll collaborate with talented professionals from our globally recognized brands—including Quadro, Fitzpatrick, Matcon, and Microfluidics—who are dedicated to solving complex manufacturing challenges.

Our commitment to trust, teamwork, and excellence empowers every team member to contribute meaningfully to help our global customers. We celebrate diversity and inclusivity, ensuring that every voice is heard and valued. If you are passionate about creative problem-solving and want to make a real impact, come and discover a rewarding career with IDEX MPT, where every day is an opportunity to excel and drive positive change.

**Technical Author**

**Overall purpose of role** :

*The purpose of this role is to draft and deliver all technical documentation for MPT Evesham products within the scope of supply. The role-holder will be required to collaborate effectively with engineers, project managers and operations team members to deliver accurate and user-friendly documentation in accordance with the project schedule. There is also a requirement to support the development of new technical publications and actively contribute to the ongoing enhancement of existing documents.*

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Draft and maintain comprehensive, user-friendly Operating Instructions, Maintenance Instructions, Installation Instructions for all Matcon equipment. Incorporate company branding in to documents.
* Assemble OEM equipment documentation for inclusion in customer documentation packs. Check supplied documentation is complete, correct and certification reflects the scope of supply and engage suppliers in the event of non-conformance.
* Compile conformity documentation for food and pharmaceutical customers including supplier part certification, quality assurance documents and equipment certification in accordance with relevant directives (eg. Machinery, ATEX, Food Hygiene etc).
* Liaise with engineering teams to incorporate design changes in to standard technical documentation. Ensure technical documentation aligns with regulatory requirements.
* Manage configuration of documentation. Ensure document revisions reflect the latest design and safety principles.
* Create and maintain technical specification documents (System Overviews, Functional Specifications) for all standard and bespoke equipment.
* Support the Design Risk Assessment process from a documentation point of view. Incorporate residual safety information in to documents in a clear and unambiguous manner.
* Create and update equipment spare parts lists. Work alongside engineering and spares teams to establish critical and wearing spare parts for standard and bespoke equipment.
* Support commercial and purchasing teams to ensure all necessary supplier documentation is identified and obtained.
* Manage translation process with external supplier for all technical documents.
* Manage material conformity documentation for stock items from suppliers. Engage suppliers to ensure conformity documentation remains current and reflects the regulations and directives applicable.

This list is not exhaustive and the job holder may be asked from time to time to undertake other duties so that the team or department can function efficiently. Such a request will be reasonable and will be within this role’s normal scope of authority.

**Skills & Abilities:**

* Strong collaborative focus with excellent communication skills showcasing the ability to extract technical information from mechanical, electrical/automation engineers and translate in to plain, user-friendly instructions for customers.
* Be aware of documentation requirements for food and pharmaceutical customers to support their validation process. Familiarity with food hygiene requirements for machinery and product contact is an advantage.

**Knowledge & Qualifications** :

* Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Technical Communications, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical experience).
* Previous experience creating and maintaining technical documentation for machinery, ideally in the food and pharmaceutical industries.
* Understanding of the Machinery Directive/Regulation, CE/UKCA marking processes and ATEX directive.
* Familiar with Microsoft Office applications, Adobe Acrobat and online document management portals. Ability to create simple drawings and graphics for inclusion in manuals.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

Join IDEX Material Processing Technologies and be part of a team that provides specialist equipment & solutions for powder material handling & blending, particle size reduction, and liquid processing for the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food, and biopharmaceutical sectors. We celebrate diversity and inclusivity, ensuring that every voice is heard and valued. If you are passionate about creative problem-solving and want to make a real impact, come and discover a rewarding career with IDEX MPT, where every day is an opportunity to excel and drive positive change.

**Controls Design Engineer**

**Overall purpose of role** :

The Controls Design Engineer is responsible for the design and development of electrical, pneumatic and functional safety systems for powder handling and process equipment applications.

The role focuses on the creation of compliant, manufacturable and supportable controls solutions from concept through detailed design, ensuring all systems meet applicable machinery safety, ATEX, cybersecurity and international compliance requirements.

Working closely with Mechanical Engineering, Operations and the Controls Software team, the Controls Design Engineer will develop robust control system architectures, technical documentation and design standards that support both project delivery and product development activities.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Controls System Design**

* Develop electrical and pneumatic control system concepts for new and existing equipment.
* Prepare detailed electrical schematics, panel layouts and manufacturing documentation.
* Design control panel architectures for UK, European and North American markets.
* Select appropriate electrical, pneumatic, instrumentation and safety components.
* Develop network architectures including Ethernet/IP, Profinet and other industrial communication systems.
* Ensure compliance with relevant electrical standards and company design practices.

**Functional Safety & Compliance**

* Lead controls-related risk reduction activities throughout the product lifecycle.
* Conduct and support risk assessments in accordance with ISO 12100.
* Design and validate safety-related control systems in accordance with ISO 13849-1.
* Produce Performance Level calculations and safety validation documentation.
* Develop safety circuit architectures including PL d and PL e systems.
* Support CE & Machinery Regulation compliance, maintain technical files and design records.

**Hazardous Area & Compliance**

* Design systems for ATEX and hazardous area applications.
* Develop and maintain ATEX documentation and supporting calculations.
* Maintain awareness of emerging legislation, standards and industry best practices and ensure all documentation complies with Quality Management System requirements.

**Documentation & Standards**

* Produce Functional Design Specifications (FDS).
* Develop and maintain standard controls design templates and documentation.
* Produce documentation suitable for manufacturing, testing, validation and customer acceptance.
* Support the creation and maintenance of company design standards.

**Product Development & Technical Support**

* Support new product development projects.
* Review customer URS documentation and develop compliant technical solutions.
* Participate in design reviews, product development, and standardisation initiatives.
* Provide technical guidance to Software Engineers, Technicians and other stakeholders.
* Provide technical support to internal stakeholders, suppliers and customers.
* Provide customer-facing technical support.

**Skills & Abilities:**

* Strong understanding of industrial control systems.
* Electrical and pneumatic system design experience.
* Knowledge of AutoCAD Electrical or equivalent design software.
* Ability to produce detailed engineering documentation.
* Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
* Strong attention to detail and commitment to engineering quality.

**Technical Knowledge:**

* Machinery Regulation (EU 2023/1230)
* EN ISO 12100 Risk Assessment & EN ISO 13849-1 Functional Safety
* Performance Level calculations and Safety circuit design
* ATEX and hazardous area system design
* Industrial cybersecurity principles (IEC 62443)
* Pneumatic design principles (ISO 4414)
* Ethernet/IP and Profinet industrial networks
* CE and UKCA compliance requirements
* UL508A / UL698A awareness

**Experience & Qualifications** :

* HNC, HND, Degree or equivalent qualification in Electrical/Controls Engineering.
* Proven Engineering experience in controls design for industrial machinery or process systems.
* Experience of electrical and pneumatic control panel design.
* Experience producing technical documentation and engineering drawings.
* Experience with ATEX and hazardous area applications.

**Training:**

· Functional training on areas such as ACAD and other software tools will be provided

· Training on internal systems and procedures specific for the role will be provided as required

· Compliance & CI training will be provided where required.

* Familiarisation with Matcon products, standards and procedures.

· Ongoing training will be agreed on as required

London

Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.

The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery.

The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you.

### **About Iso**

Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.

Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.

Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.

### **Your impact**

At Isomorphic Labs, DMPK Leads drive the DMPK strategy of drug discovery projects to deliver high quality clinical candidates whilst using and contributing to the optimisation of state-of-the-art computational and AI ADME models.

As part of the Drug Design and Medical Research team and through close collaboration with the Technology teams, you will be supporting the business alongside world leading AI/ML Drug Design Platform teams. You will collaborate to deliver scientific expertise and strategic direction to drive both improvements in the Platform and apply this to real drug design projects.

If you are a skilled and ambitious scientist looking to take the next step in your career, joining Isomorphic Labs will lift you out of your comfort zone and provide you with an amazing opportunity for personal growth and development.

* Experience with biologics, peptides and other new modalities.

* Utilise state-of-the-art modelling (e.g., ML/AI and PBPK) to extrapolate preclinical data and predict human dosing, efficacy, and safety windows

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants their models in production under real conditions — bad lighting, awkward camera angles, crowded aisles — rather than on a benchmark leaderboard.

* Own the detection pipeline end-to-end: person detection, multi-object tracking, re-identification, and behaviour classification.

* Drive down false positives — the single metric that decides whether a retailer keeps the system switched on.
* Optimise inference to run reliably on in-store hardware, balancing accuracy against frame rate and cost.
