Stock options: Everyone who joins and contributes to Reflection's success gets to share in the upside through stock options.

# Verification, Validation and Test Engineer

**About Rimac Energy**

Rimac Energy is a rapidly growing division of Rimac Group, developing next-generation battery energy storage and power conversion technology for grid-scale and commercial energy applications. Building on Rimac’s expertise in battery systems, power electronics and software, we are developing highly integrated BESS and PCS products for deployment across global markets, with an initial focus on the United States followed by Europe.

We are seeking an experienced Verification, Validation and Test (VVT) Engineer to take ownership of test engineering for our energy storage products. You will plan and run verification and validation campaigns, own failure analysis, and make sure every test produces the traceable evidence needed for certification. This role carries forward established test methods and knowledge through a structured handover, so you will join early enough to learn the existing rigs, procedures and certification approach before taking full ownership. The ideal candidate combines hands-on test experience with high-voltage battery and power electronics systems, a disciplined approach to evidence, and a passion for sustainable energy.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Own the verification and validation test plans for products, from requirements and test specifications through to final reports.
* Take over and maintain the certification test methods, keeping procedures, test cases and acceptance criteria current and repeatable.
* Carry out performance, reliability, safety and environmental testing on battery, power electronics and system-level hardware.
* Lead failure analysis and root-cause investigations, working with design, integration and software teams to close issues and confirm fixes through retest.
* Produce clear, auditable test evidence and reports that support certification submissions and technical files, working closely with the Compliance Engineer.
* Maintain traceability between requirements, test cases and results so that test outcomes can be shown against the relevant standards.
* Define rig, fixture and instrumentation requirements, and direct test technicians in rig preparation, safe operation and data collection.
* Develop and improve test automation and data analysis using tools such as Python and LabVIEW.
* Support testing at external certification laboratories and test facilities, and act as a technical point of contact during witness testing.
* Communicate test progress, risks and results to engineering leads and programme stakeholders.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
* Proven experience in verification, validation or test of battery energy storage systems, power electronics or similar high-voltage products.
* Experience producing test evidence for product certification, and familiarity with relevant standards (for example IEC 62619, IEC 62477, UL 1973 / UL 9540 or grid codes).
* Strong failure analysis and root-cause problem-solving skills (for example 8D, fishbone or fault tree analysis).
* Strong understanding of test methodologies, instrumentation, data acquisition and monitoring tools.
* Experience with test automation and scripting, ideally Python and/or LabVIEW.
* Safe working practices for high-voltage systems; HV qualification or willingness to obtain one.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a disciplined approach to documentation.
* Desirable: experience of a test lab handover or building up a test function, and of directing technicians.

**What we are like and what we offer**

* **Technically challenging, high-impact work** on advanced energy storage and power conversion products — from concept through prototype, validation, and production
* **A collaborative, cross-functional engineering culture** with strong links between mechanical, electrical, controls, software, compliance, CAE, test, supply chain, and manufacturing
* **Fast-paced environment** where practical problem-solving and initiative are genuinely valued
* **Continuous learning and development**, with exposure to rapidly evolving energy and power electronics technology
* **A friendly, ambitious team** that works hard and takes pride in what it builds
* **Educational budget –** at Rimac Energy, we believe in the importance of continuous learning. We provide an educational budget to support your growth, and we actively encourage you to expand your knowledge and skills.

## Description

The Ring Video Platform Team innovates in the video streaming space for Ring cameras. We are passionate about helping customers see what matters at home, whenever they need to. Every day, millions of Ring devices stream, record and process video through services we build and operate. At that scale we hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, latency, video quality and privacy.

We're looking for a technically deep Software Development Manager to lead one of our video platform teams. This role suits someone who enjoys the engineering as much as the people side. We're also changing how we build software. AI is becoming part of every stage of our development lifecycle, from design and coding through review, testing and operations. You'll help shape what that looks like in practice. That means working out where AI genuinely makes engineers more effective, building it into the team's daily workflow, and using it to raise the quality bar as well as the pace.

The Ring Video Platform organization, based in Cambridge/London, builds and operates the cloud services that power Ring video, from the moment a camera starts streaming to when a customer watches it on their phone. You will be key in the day-to-day running of one of our supported housing services. We don’t run care homes, so there’s no need to provide personal care. The priority in your role includes the safety and wellbeing of everyone in our accommodation, including our customers.   
Working with people who have a range of needs, you could be doing any number of things. From supporting customers in conversations with calls from their GP, Social Services, or benefits teams – to dealing with the emergency services including the Police and Ambulance, when the need arises.   
You’ll log all incidents to make sure we have an accurate record of events. And when a customer leaves, you will clean and prepare their room, ready for the next occupant.   
  
**About you**  
We are looking for someone with:   
•  Experience of working with people in a customer facing environment.   
•  An understanding of supporting vulnerable people – this could include having your own lived experience of homelessness or drug or alcohol addiction.   
•  Basic administrative and IT skills and attention to detail are required to maintain records and in-house systems.   
  
**Why Riverside?**  
At Riverside, we’re a housing association with a difference – enhancing the everyday for all our customers. For 90 years, we’ve been revitalising neighbourhoods and supporting communities by providing the homes they need to live full, fulfilling and rewarding lives.    
We have a portfolio of over 75,000 affordable residential and retirement homes across the UK. Our work ranges from homelessness services to social care, employment support to retirement living, and we need the best people on board to help us.   
  
Working with us, you’ll enjoy:   
•  Competitive pay & generous pension    
•  25 days holidays plus bank holidays   
•  Investment in your learning, personal development and technology   
•  A wide range of benefits    
  
**Diversity and Inclusion at Riverside:**  
We are inclusive. At Riverside, we value diversity in all its forms. We foster a workplace where all individuals are respected, empowered, and heard. Our commitment to inclusivity drives our success and enriches the lives of our customers and colleagues.

**Role Profile**  
Support customers

**About the team**

The Financial Reporting team protects the integrity of consolidated financial reporting across Argos. The team leads periodic and year-end consolidation, statutory reporting, technical accounting and accounting policy, providing high-quality financial information to senior management, the Board, shareholders, lenders and external auditors. This is a central Finance role with visibility across the business and the opportunity to influence strategic decisions through clear, reliable reporting and practical technical advice.

**More about the role**

As Finance Manager – Financial and Technical Reporting, you will own delivery of accurate, timely consolidated financial statements, supporting schedules and reporting packs. **More about you**

You will be a qualified accountant with demonstrable experience of Group consolidation, UK-adopted international accounting standards and UK statutory reporting. You will be able to apply technical guidance to complex or material transactions and communicate the accounting implications in concise, commercially relevant language. Experience of significant transactions or business change will help you identify issues early and support informed decisions.

You will combine technical judgement with a hands-on approach to delivery. You will be comfortable coordinating demanding reporting timetables, working with auditors and senior stakeholders, and maintaining accuracy when priorities compete. You will also bring evidence of coaching or managing others, setting clear priorities and improving reporting processes, controls or systems.

**Essential criteria**

* ACA qualification, or an equivalent recognised professional accountancy qualification.
* Demonstrable experience of owning Group consolidation, including legal entity submissions, consolidation adjustments, intercompany eliminations and consolidated financial statement preparation.
* Practical knowledge of UK-adopted international accounting standards, the Companies Act and UK statutory reporting requirements, evidenced through preparation or review of statutory financial statements.
* Evidence of preparing technical accounting papers for complex or material transactions, setting out relevant guidance, judgements, financial impacts and a recommended treatment.
* Proven experience of managing an external audit or Group reporting timetable and coaching or managing at least one finance colleague.

## Job Description

**As part of the application process, please submit a cover letter addressing the following question:**

**"What is your proudest moment advancing agility in a team? Tell us what you did, and one thing you learnt."**

**About us**

Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We serve a diverse client base that includes pension schemes, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, high net worth individuals, family offices, as well as end clients through partnerships with distributors, financial advisers, and online platforms.

Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.

**Role purpose**

The Delivery Lead is a coaching-style delivery role that consolidates the different delivery streams across the Enterprise Technology function into a single point of delivery accountability. The role exists to bring consistency, pace and quality to how the function delivers - by coaching teams, raising delivery practice to a common standard, getting hands-on where it adds most value, and holding end-to-end accountability for delivery outcomes across the function.

The role also plays a direct part in the Superhighway programme, Schroders' agentic-development initiative, helping shape and land the way teams deliver in an increasingly agentic engineering environment.

This is a leadership role that leads primarily through influence, coaching and delivery expertise rather than through direct line management alone. It suits someone who is equally comfortable shaping a delivery operating model at the function level and rolling their sleeves up inside a team when the situation calls for it.

**Key accountabilities**

**1. Coach teams and raise delivery to a common standard**

* Coach delivery teams across the function - including delivery leads, engineers and product/BA colleagues - to strengthen how they plan, prioritise, sequence and ship work.
* Establish and embed a consistent, lightweight delivery standard across streams, so teams work to shared, well-understood practices without unnecessary process.
* Identify where teams are below standard and bring them up through hands-on coaching, pairing and practical support rather than mandate.
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement, learning and openness to feedback across delivery teams.

**2. Get hands-on in delivery where it adds most value**

* Step directly into delivery when a team needs it - unblocking, structuring the work, facilitating, or leading a critical piece through to completion.
* Model good delivery practice by doing, so coaching is grounded in credibility and current practice.
* Deploy hands-on effort deliberately and proportionately, keeping the focus on building lasting team capability rather than creating dependency.

**3. Hold end-to-end accountability for delivery across the function**

* Act as the single point of accountability for delivery across the Enterprise Technology function, giving leadership a clear, consolidated view of delivery status, risk and progress.
* Consolidate visibility across delivery streams - milestones, dependencies, risks and run-the-bank commitments - into a coherent picture that supports decision-making.
* Establish and maintain the governance, reporting and decision-making mechanisms that keep delivery accountable, transparent and on track.
* Manage complexity, ambiguity and cross-team dependencies, removing systemic obstacles so teams can deliver.
* Ensure delivery is aligned to the function's strategy, priorities and value objectives.

**4. Play a direct role in the Superhighway agentic-development programme**

* Contribute directly to the Superhighway programme, shaping and landing the delivery approach for agentic software development at Schroders.
* Help teams adopt agentic ways of working safely and effectively, translating new engineering approaches into practical, governed delivery practice.
* Ensure delivery practices scale and adapt as the engineering model evolves, keeping guardrails and standards fit for an agentic environment.

**Experience, knowledge and attributes**

**Essential**

* Substantial experience leading delivery across multiple teams or streams in a technology function, with a track record of raising delivery standards.
* A genuine coaching orientation - able to build capability in others and lead through influence, not just direction.
* Credible hands-on delivery background - comfortable stepping into the detail of planning, facilitation and shipping when needed.
* Strong command of modern delivery practice (Agile and Lean), applied pragmatically rather than dogmatically.
* Proven ability to manage complexity, ambiguity and cross-team dependencies in a large or federated technology estate.
* Confident establishing governance, reporting and delivery transparency for a leadership audience.
* Strong stakeholder management and communication across technical and senior stakeholders.

**Desirable**

* Experience in enterprise platform, data platform or engineering-enablement environments.
* Familiarity with agentic / AI-assisted software development and its implications for the delivery model.
* Exposure to regulated financial services delivery and its governance expectations.

**Attributes**

* Action-oriented and pragmatic; optimises for outcomes and alignment over process.
* Builds trust quickly and coaches with credibility.
* Comfortable moving between function-level strategy and team-level detail.
* Resilient and adaptable in a fast-changing engineering environment.

**What success looks like**

* Delivery streams across the function work to a consistent, well-understood standard, with teams visibly more capable over time.
* Leadership has a single, trusted view of delivery status, risk and progress across the function.
* Teams that were below standard are measurably stronger, with dependency less on the role holder over time.
* Delivery keeps pace as the function adopts agentic engineering practices, with guardrails and standards that scale.
* The delivery operating model adapts as the function and its technology evolve.

We’re the specialist lender for the real economy. Businesses that make and build things, homes people live in, and savers whose money works hard for them.

We offer a diverse range of savings and loan products. From personal and business savings accounts and loans for new cars, to complex financial credit facilities for businesses requiring significant investment and mortgages for landlords with multiple properties – no two customers are ever the same.

Customers come to us when there’s a lot riding on it, the options are complicated and the clock is ticking. We take the time to understand what’s really going on, make a call and stand behind it. Technology takes care of the routine work, so you spend your time where judgement makes the difference.

***How we work***

* **Think deeper**: Skills matter more than job titles. Never settle for “that’ll do”.
* **Own it**: Don’t wait to be asked. If you spot a problem, fix it.
* **One Shawbrook**: Lots of brands, one team. Share what you know, wherever you sit.

**If you are ready to take ownership, contribute new ideas and help make things real, you are our kind of person. Work with us because you:**

* Want to be part of the best specialist lender for the economy, driving real growth across the UK.
* Never stand still and enjoy an ambitious, hardworking culture where we predict change and adapt fast.
* Think deeper, don’t assume and never settle for standard. You look beyond the obvious, apply critical judgement and find better ways to solve complex problems.
* Want to own it, work constructively with others and make decisions that you commit to and drive through to action.

Shawbrook’s ACA Finance programme will kick start your career, gaining experience and insight into the Finance department and the broader business over your 3-year programme.

In the 3-year programme, you will rotate across various Finance functions such as Financial Control, Financial Planning & Analysis, Mergers & Acquisitions and Treasury, gaining real world experience while aligning to the ACA qualification. You will have a manager within each of your rotations and a mentor who will support you throughout the programme.

You will study for your ACA qualification (ICAEW) covering up to 14 exams over the 3-year programme. We also support you through BPP, our study support partner who will help you with training for the exams and we offer you time off from work to focus on studying for your exams.

The rounded experience and ACA qualification will open up a wide range of opportunities into one of our departments within finance where you will be able to hone your financial skills further, enabling you to become a Finance leader of the future.

* Excellent interpersonal skills.

* Manage and provide out of hours Water Quality advice, reporting and liaison arrangements.

* Implement and further improve the quality management systems, including the adoption of best working practices

* Knowledge of quality management systems and regulatory audit processes.
* Experience supporting operational incidents and emergency response activities.
* Chartered status or working towards professional accreditation with a recognised scientific body.

## What We Offer

At South West Water, our people are the heart of everything we do. We believe in creating an environment where everyone can thrive, bring their best every day, and feel truly valued. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your wellbeing, career and financial future.

**The role**  
  
The Retention & Recovery Lead owns one pipeline that follows every merchant from the first sign they might leave, through retention, a well-run exit and collections, to write-off or debt sale.  
  
Today we treat churn and collections as separate problems, and neither has a clear owner. In practice they are usually the same merchant at different points in time: a merchant who goes quiet in March becomes, by June, an unpaid fee, a terminal still in the field and a balance nobody is chasing. Collections activity also sits in pockets across the business, from unpaid subscriptions and fees, negative balances and chargebacks to terminal recovery, dissolved companies and fraud losses. As our credit products grow, so will the need.  
  
You’ll bring all of this together under one strategy, one queue and one set of metrics. We want someone who knows collections and its pain points, and who approaches the whole lifecycle with a product and design mindset: redesigning journeys end to end, and deciding where AI and automation belong and where people add the most value. You’ll start hands-on and build a small credit control team as the capability grows.  
  
**What you’ll do**

* Own the retention-to-recovery pipeline end to end, from the first churn signal to write-off or debt sale, running from one prioritised queue with one set of definitions.
* Work with our data team to build and run an AI retention engine that identifies merchants heading towards churn, recommends the next best action for each and puts them in a queue to be worked. Prove what works with holdout groups, and do more of it.
* Agree with Commercial how save conversations are delivered, and make sure our own risk actions, such as held settlements, are weighed before they push a good merchant out.
* Design a proper exit for every merchant who leaves: a recorded reason, fees stopped, terminal returned, final balance netted and a final statement, so merchants do not need to contact Customer Relations to close their account.
* Build automated collections that start the day a balance turns negative: settlement netting, direct debit, card on file, payment links and payment plans. Journeys run through the Teya app and portal first, with phone as the exception.
* Run managed and external recovery for larger balances: credit control, payment plans, an agency panel, write-off thresholds and, as a last resort, debt sale.
* Own the recovery strategy for fraud-related balances with Fraud Operations and Legal. They keep investigation and legal action; you make sure every balance has a recovery route and a priority.
* Run the existing book as a separate remediation project with its own end date, so it does not pull focus from the new flow.
* Connect the work of Billing, Payments, Logistics (terminal recovery), Credit, Customer Relations and the termination and withheld funds process into one joined-up flow.
* Define and own the pipeline’s metrics, report them monthly, and feed what you learn back into onboarding, pricing and risk policy.
* Prepare the capability to scale with Teya’s growing credit book, and hire and lead the credit control team.

**In your first six months**

* Definitions agreed and reported for flow recovery rate, stock recovery rate and true churn.
* A single queue live, worked by hand from simple rules while the model is built.
* An exit process in place for every leaving merchant, and an automated collections first version running in at least one market.
* The credit control team hired or in hiring, and the legacy book project under way with a clear plan.

**By the end of your first year**

* The first retention model live, beating the rules-based baseline and tested against holdout groups.
* Flow recovery rate by day 90 tracking towards our 70% target, with time to recovery and cost to collect reported monthly.
* The first debt sale completed, where the legal and data preconditions are met.
* Measurably fewer Customer Relations contacts from merchants who are leaving or owe us money.

# Level Designer

### Level designers lay out the spaces a game is played in and tune how they read, how they flow and how hard they are.

A level designer builds the playable space: the layout of an area, the route a player takes through it, the placement of encounters, cover, pickups and the signposting that makes all of it readable. The work starts in blockout, where only volumes and distances exist, and ends after many rounds of playtesting, where pacing and difficulty are adjusted against what players actually do rather than what the plan assumed.

Most of the job happens inside an editor. Postings ask for scripting of events and triggers, visual scripting such as Blueprints, world building across connected areas, and enough technical care to keep an area inside its performance budget.

The neighbouring roles split along two lines. A level artist dresses and lights the space the level designer has laid out; a game designer owns the rules and systems the space is built around. Level design sits between them and answers for the experience of moving through the world.

**Senior Manager, Environmental Services for the Mining Industry**

**About Palladium:**  
Operating in over 50 countries, Palladium
is a global consulting and implementation company working in partnership with
governments, businesses, investors, and communities to design and deliver
solutions that create lasting positive impact. We address some of the world’s
most complex challenges across infrastructure, economic growth and natural
capital, health, energy, climate and environment, and digital
transformation—strengthening systems, institutions, and markets to support
inclusive and sustainable development. Our more than 2,100 staff worldwide work
as trusted advisors across diverse contexts, combining deep technical
expertise, implementation techniques, and innovative technology to deliver
locally informed, client-focused solutions that help organizations achieve
measurable, sustainable impact.

Palladium is
part of GISI’s global family of companies, which aims to create solutions for
the world’s most complex challenges. With annual revenues of $14 billion,
GISI’s approximately 15,000 employees are engaged in projects across 100
countries worldwide providing construction, program/project management, and
engineering consulting services.  
  
**This Opportunity:**  
  
The Sustainable Infrastructure team, part of the broader Economic
Growth & Natural Capital (EGNC) Portfolio based in Palladium's Americas region, partners with mining companies
to design and implement positive impact programs—such as workforce skilling,
reforestation, and sustainable agriculture—that benefit mining communities and
regions. The team works across the entire mining life cycle, helping clients
achieve ESG targets while building the foundation for community resilience
beyond mine closure. The team draws on expertise from the wider EGNC portfolio,
which also works with private sector clients as well as philanthropic bodies
and diverse donors (IDB, USDA, AFD, WB) to support agricultural value chain
development, enhance women’s access to finance, and mobilize capital for
climate-positive initiatives. Overall, the business seeks to unlock and scale
innovative solutions that drive inclusive growth and deliver sustainable value
for communities  
  
Palladium is
seeking a **Senior Manager, Environmental Services for the Mining Industry**to
lead team management and provide technical expertise across business
development and project delivery in environmental risk management, impact
strategy, and implementation, particularly within mining, infrastructure,
climate, and nature-based solutions. The role requires strong expertise in
environmental risks in mining, including experience designing and implementing
environmental management plans, and overseeing biodiversity, decarbonization,
major hazards, tailings, waste, water, air, and rehabilitation initiatives.
Candidates should have experience in the closure phase of the asset lifecycle,
including Post Mining Land Use planning and program design, and demonstrate a
track record of working with diverse mining clients in North America. The
position also supports business development efforts such as strategic planning,
pipeline forecasting, proposal development, partnerships, networking, and
recruitment. **Fluency in English and one additional language – French,
Spanish, or Portuguese is required.**  
  
**Location:**  
  
The position can be based out of **Palladium’s London office.** Applicants
must have current/future work authorization in the UK as visa sponsorship
cannot be provided.

This role is also posted in the US; however, there is only one position available.

**Reporting Lines:**

* This role reports to the Director, Sustainable Infrastructure (UK based)

**Primary
Roles and Responsibilities:**  
  
 *Project Management*

* Lead multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality, client-focused results across complex assignments
* Oversee proposal development, budgeting, project planning, implementation, and reporting to ensure timely and effective delivery
* Identify, engage, and manage partners and subcontractors to strengthen technical quality and delivery capacity
* Manage partner and subcontractor performance to ensure contractually compliant delivery of agreed inputs, outputs, and outcomes
* Serve as Project Director, providing quality assurance for deliverables and oversight of budgets, client relationships, and overall project performance

*Business Development* 

* Contribute to the
  identification, assessment, and pursuit of new business opportunities with
  a focus on opening business with new clients and broadening Palladium’s
  work in the closure and environmental performance space and ability to
  leverage their own network activating new client portfolios quickly
* Contribute to the preparation of technical
  proposals principally targeting private sector and blended finance
  opportunities with mining sector clients (focus on impact program design
  & implementation, work with standards setting bodies to enhance community
  resilience requirements, closure and post mining land use engagements, and
  integrated environmental risk and management support etc.)

*Technical Work*

* Work with the team to develop short-term inputs
  and/or consultancy assignments on topics such as environmental risk
  management, biodiversity, decarbonization, major hazards, tailings, waste,
  water, air quality, rehabilitation, regional economic development, climate
  finance and nature-based solutions
* Lead
  technical input into the design, planning and delivery of environmental
  and socioeconomic impact initiatives driven by mining companies, including
  the development and implementation of environmental management plans and
  systems that also engage private sector, impact funders or development
  organizations to co-invest in positive impact
* Contribute
  to research, analysis and publication of technical reports, case studies,
  policy/program approaches, and results summaries on themes related to
  environmental risk, community resilience, regional economic development,
  post mining land use, closure, rehabilitation, and social and just
  transition in emerging markets
* Help to identify, build, and maintain
  relationships with partners and consultants that can provide environmental
  and technical expertise to Palladium-managed projects
* Stay current on trends and tendencies in the
  mining sector and track structural, governance and ESG target changes for
  key clients, including evolving expectations on biodiversity,
  decarbonization, tailings, waste, water and closure
* Work
  with others in the EGNC Portfolio to promote and build Palladium’s
  technical capability, especially regarding integrated environmental and
  socioeconomic work with mining companies

**Essential
Criteria:**

* **5+ years working directly with mining companies as clients**
* **Fluency in English and at least one other language, in either French, Spanish, or Portuguese**
* Masters in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, Economics, Anthropology, Sociology, Business Administration, International Development, Politics or related discipline preferred
* Strong networks in the mining and minerals sector
* Preference for experience managing teams across
  geographies and cultures
* Proven experience in or on
  emerging market issues and/or contexts
* Experience leading business
  development efforts
* Strong environmental background, including understanding of environmental risks in the mining context and demonstrated experience leading the design and implementation of environmental management plans and/or managing biodiversity, decarbonization, major hazards, tailings, waste, water, air, and rehabilitation efforts
* In-house experience working for a mining company preferred

* Excellent

Thomson Reuters is seeking an experienced, commercially minded, and people-focused **Assistant General Counsel** **- Group Data Protection Officer** to join our Legal & Privacy function. Reporting directly to the Chief Privacy Officer, this senior leadership role will be integral to advancing Thomson Reuters' global privacy strategy, leading a geographically distributed team of privacy lawyers, and ensuring robust data protection and cybersecurity legal compliance across our worldwide operations.

  

This is a unique opportunity for a privacy leader who thrives at the intersection of law, technology, and global regulatory complexity — someone who can inspire and develop a high-performing team while shaping strategy and delivering practical, business-enabling legal guidance at scale.

  

As Thomson Reuters accelerates its investment in AI-powered products and services built to the highest standards of trust and responsibility, this role will be at the forefront of defining how fiduciary-grade AI technology is developed, governed, and deployed in compliance with evolving global data protection and cybersecurity frameworks.

  

Key Responsibilities 

Statutory Data Protection Officer Duties 

* Serve as the designated Data Protection Officer under UK GDPR and EU GDPR, fulfilling all statutory duties including independent monitoring of compliance, providing advice on DPIAs, and acting as the primary point of contact for supervisory authorities.

* Maintain the independence and direct reporting line required of the statutory DPO function, escalating matters directly to the Board or highest level of management where required.

* Champion privacy-by-design principles across the business, ensuring privacy considerations are embedded in product, technology, and business strategy decisions at the executive level.

 

Global Privacy Function Oversight 

* Provide oversight and accountability for the Privacy Operations Lead function, including the global privacy program’s operational governance, strategic roadmap, cyber incident management coordination, and leadership of privacy operations specialists and privacy engineers.

* Provide senior oversight of specialized legal counsel functions reporting into the privacy organization, including Senior Counsel, US Government Privacy Compliance (FedRAMP, CMMC, and federal privacy program advisory) and Senior Counsel, Cyber Security & Privacy (global incident response, breach notification, and EU/APAC cybersecurity regulatory advisory), ensuring consistency of legal position across the organization and clear escalation into DPO-level governance.

* Provide executive oversight of the Senior Privacy Operations Analyst and Senior Privacy Operations Engineer functions globally, ensuring the operational and technical backbone of the privacy program (data mapping/ROPA infrastructure, DSAR and assessment automation, KPI and risk reporting) is resourced appropriately and aligns with the DPO’s governance framework and risk appetite.

* Establish and maintain a Group-wide escalation framework ensuring that material legal, regulatory, or operational privacy risk identified at any level of the privacy organization - whether in legal counsel, operations, or engineering - is escalated to the DPO in a timely and consistent manner.

 

Regulatory Relationships & Incident Governance 

* Serve as primary liaison with data protection authorities, including managing regulatory inquiries, audits, and investigations.

* Oversee the company’s response to significant data breaches from a governance and regulatory notification perspective, including final sign-off on regulator and data subject notification strategy for high-severity incidents.

 

Board & Executive Reporting 

* Report regularly to Chief Privacy Officer and relevant Board and Audit committees on privacy risk, regulatory developments, and program maturity across all privacy functions.

* Provide the Board, Audit Committee and Chief Privacy Officer with a consolidated, enterprise-wide view of privacy risk spanning legal, operations, and engineering functions.

 

 

Regulatory Horizon Scanning 

* Monitor global privacy regulatory developments and ensure the organization’s program, operating model, and resourcing evolve to meet new and emerging requirements.

* Direct horizon-scanning activity performed across the privacy legal, operations, and engineering functions, ensuring material regulatory developments are translated into updated policy, playbooks, and technical controls at the appropriate level of the organization.

 

Required Qualifications 

* Extensive experience (typically 12+ years) in data protection/privacy law or privacy leadership roles, including prior experience serving as a DPO or in a senior privacy leadership capacity at Director level or above.

* Deep expertise in UK GDPR and EU GDPR, including the statutory role and independence requirements of the DPO function.

* Demonstrated experience managing regulatory relationships and/or investigations with data protection authorities.

* Proven Director-level leadership experience building and managing global, multi-region privacy teams spanning multiple disciplines, including legal counsel, privacy operations, and privacy engineering functions.

* Demonstrated experience overseeing distinct specialized functions (e.g., government/regulatory legal counsel, cybersecurity incident response counsel, privacy operations, and privacy engineering) within a single, unified governance framework.

* Law degree and/or relevant professional qualification preferred; CIPP/E and/or CIPM strongly preferred.

 

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience advising on privacy matters related to AI/automated decision-making.

* Experience overseeing both legal/compliance and technical/engineering functions within a single organizational structure.

For more than a century, Kenyon International Emergency Services has been the organisation that airlines, governments and major companies call on to make sure that happens.

We are looking for a senior crisis leader to direct that response across the UK, Europe and Africa. This is a role for someone who has stood in the room when it mattered, who leads with calm authority, and who believes that how an organisation treats the bereaved and the injured says everything about its character.

**About Kenyon**

Kenyon provides emergency planning, family assistance, humanitarian support and recovery services to clients around the world, drawing on a network of more than 2,500 trained responders who can be mobilised at short notice into any jurisdiction. Our clients rely on us to keep their promises to the people affected by an incident, and we hold ourselves to that standard every day, not only on the day of an activation.

Kenyon is part of the TrustFlight Group, an aviation safety and compliance technology business. That gives Kenyon something unusual in this sector: a world class technology team working alongside it, and a genuine commitment to using AI to make crisis response faster, better informed and more humane. Our values are simple and we mean them: integrity, and a customer first attitude in everything we do.

**The role**

Kenyon operates a two hub leadership model. You will lead the Bracknell hub, with regional accountability for operational delivery, readiness, contracted offices and relationships across the UK, Europe and Africa. Your peer, the Regional Director of Operations in Vancouver, leads the Americas and Asia Pacific. Together you share accountability for the readiness and quality of Kenyon’s response worldwide.

**Senior Incident Director for activations**

Senior on call duty is shared between the two Directors on a fixed twelve hour rota, with a structured handover at each change of duty, so that cover is continuous around the clock and neither Director works through their own night. Your window runs from approximately 06:00 to 18:00 UK time.

When an incident arises during your window, wherever in the world it occurs, you take up the role of Senior Incident Director. You will have the authority to set the deployment posture, commit responders and stand the organisation up or down without further approval. Where a client requires it, you will deploy as their strategic point of contact, leading the response on their behalf at the most demanding moments an organisation can face, including mass casualty, government led and politically sensitive events.

Major activations are infrequent, and Kenyon holds its capability through a surge based model rather than a large permanent workforce. Your judgement of regional readiness, kept current every week of the year, is what makes that model work.

**What you will lead**

·       **Regional readiness and response.** Maintain and continuously measure activation readiness across the UK, Europe and Africa, and develop the procedures, protocols and contingency plans that underpin it.

·       **Your team and offices.** Line manage the Regional Operations Manager in Bracknell, run the Bracknell hub and its regional operations as one regional function, and hold contracted offices to defined standards through quarterly reviews and an annual assessment.

·       **Protecting those we serve.** Make sure the information of casualties, families and clients is protected with the same care during and after an activation as on any other day.

·       **The responder network.** Work with the Responder Manager to keep the network vetted, trained and available across the region, including building language capable responders across Europe and Africa. Own the global standards for responder vetting, training currency, deployment conduct and post incident review, ensuring they are consistently applied across both hubs.

·       **AI and digital quality assurance.** Work with the Vancouver Director and TrustFlight Group technology team to define and evaluate AI enabled quality and operational reporting tools, including an AI internal auditor supporting ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 22300 evidence gathering, gap identification and audit trail maintenance. Ensure these tools meet group information security, data governance and ethical standards.

·       **Global operational standards.** Work with the Vancouver Director to compare regional procedures, share lessons learned and adopt improvements across both hubs, ensuring consistent service quality while recognising regional operational requirements.

·       **Relationships that matter.** Build trusted working relationships with government agencies, emergency services, aviation authorities and clients across the region, and provide the operational insight that informs board level reporting.

**Why join us**

·       **Work that matters.** Few roles offer the chance to lead a service whose sole purpose is to bring order, care and dignity to people at the worst moment of their lives.

·       **Real authority.** A senior seat on the Kenyon leadership team, reporting to the Managing Director, with decision making authority during activations.

·       **A sustainable model.** A shared rota designed so that no Director carries standing 24/7 availability, because sound judgement depends on rest.

·       **Room to build.** The opportunity to shape Kenyon’s growth across the UK, Europe and Africa, while leading the development of global quality, certification and responder standards and helping shape how AI strengthens operational assurance across Kenyon.

In your cover letter, tell us about an incident you have led and what it taught you about caring for the people affected. Applications will be treated in strict confidence.

*Kenyon International Emergency Services and TrustFlight are equal opportunity employers. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process for anyone who needs them. This position is employed by Kenyon International Emergency Services Limited.*

## Job requirements

**What you will bring**

·       At least ten years in operational crisis management or emergency response, including five or more in a leadership role.

·       Experience leading large scale or complex incident responses in international environments, ideally including direct responsibility for strategic command.

·       A track record of managing contracted service providers against defined performance standards.

·       Experience working within a quality management framework in a regulated or standards led environment, and alongside board level governance.

·       The composure, judgement and compassion to lead when the stakes are highest, and the humility to put the needs of affected families first.

·       Willingness to travel internationally at short notice, including to the United States and across Asia Pacific.

·       Eligibility to live and work in the UK.

**It would be a real advantage if you also have**

·       Professional fluency in Spanish, or another principal European and African language.

·       Familiarity with the ISO 22300 series, including ISO 22320, or equivalent certification experience.

·       Experience overseeing a 24/7 contact centre operation.

·       Practical experience commissioning AI or automation tools in an operational setting.

·       Knowledge of the aviation, maritime, energy or government crisis response markets in the Europe and Africa.

# Overnight Mental Health Crisis Peer Support Worker

### Job Introduction

Our Recovery Lounge in Manchester was first commissioned in 2021 and has provided vital evening support to people across the city for the past five years. During this time, we have developed a strong track record of supporting people in mental health crisis who are seeking immediate support.

Due to the success of the service, we are now extending our opening hours to provide overnight support. This exciting new project is initially funded for 12 months, with a further two years of funding already earmarked subject to successful delivery. We are now recruiting a dedicated team to help shape and deliver this enhanced service.

**The Role**

As an Overnight Peer Support Worker, you'll be at the heart of the service, providing emotional and practical support to people who may be experiencing emotional distress or a mental health crisis.

Drawing on your own lived experience of mental health challenges and recovery, you will use this experience appropriately to inspire hope, build trust and support people accessing the service. Your ability to share aspects of your recovery journey in a safe and professional way will help people feel understood, empowered and less alone in their experiences.

Working in an environment where no two shifts are the same, you'll help create a safe, welcoming and supportive space where people feel listened to, understood and empowered to move forward.

You'll work alongside colleagues to support individuals accessing the service, helping them explore coping strategies, build resilience and identify positive next steps as part of their recovery journey.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide compassionate, recovery-focused support to individuals experiencing a mental health crisis.
* Build positive and supportive relationships with individuals accessing the service.
* Use your lived experience in a safe, purposeful and professional way to support and encourage others in their recovery.
* Undertake triage assessments to identify individuals' needs and determine the most appropriate support.
* Complete risk assessments and contribute to ongoing risk management plans.
* Identify and respond appropriately to risk, safeguarding concerns and crisis situations.
* Offer emotional support and encouragement to help people manage difficult situations and work towards their recovery goals.
* Support individuals to identify their strengths, develop coping strategies and make informed choices about their wellbeing.
* Promote hope, independence and self-confidence through meaningful engagement and person-centred support.
* Maintain accurate and timely records in line with GDPR and organisational requirements.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues and partner agencies to ensure the best outcomes for service users.
* Contribute to the smooth running of the service, including general housekeeping duties to maintain a comfortable and welcoming environment.
* Promote a safe, inclusive and welcoming environment where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.

**About You**

We're looking for passionate, resilient and empathetic individuals who are committed to supporting people with mental health needs.

You will ideally have:

* Lived experience of mental health challenges, emotional distress or crisis, and experience of recovery.

Head of Product Delivery

Permanent (E) · Hybrid · London Studio, United Kingdom

Overview

Application

About this job

About the role

ustwo is looking for a Head of Product Delivery to build something that doesn’t exist here yet.  
  
We make exceptional digital products with our clients, bringing strategy, product, design, research and engineering together to solve genuinely hard problems. Product and Delivery have been two separate disciplines here. The market has moved, the work we’re being asked to do has changed shape, and the two are far more useful to our clients together than apart. So we’re bringing them into a single Product Delivery discipline, and we’re handing it to someone who’ll make it their own.  
  
Product Delivery are the orchestrators. They hold the destination and the route to it, along with every building block in between, and they lead the team and often the client all the way there. That means product strategy, roadmaps and the story work that turns an ambition into something a team can build, alongside shaping and pricing the engagement, then holding scope and change when things get complicated. Design, Strategy and Engineering work alongside them at every step.  
  
It’s a brand new role, and that’s the best part of it. You’ll shape the discipline at the same time as you run it, alongside a team already doing strong work for clients. What product delivery means at ustwo, what great looks like and how we know whether it worked are all yours to answer, and not many roles let you start from a blank page that size.  
  
This is a leadership role above all else. Your impact comes through the discipline and the people in it rather than the engagements you personally run, though we’d expect you in the work often enough to set the standard by example, particularly early on. You’ll bring a clear point of view on where product practice is heading and the appetite to get your hands into the work rather than describing it from a distance.  
  
**Where the role sits**  
The discipline will be around twelve people, spread across London, Malmö and New York, so you’ll be leading people you won’t sit next to. That takes a particular kind of leadership: clear enough that people can act without you in the room, present enough that they never feel managed from a distance. Regular travel to the other studios comes with the job as you embed new ways of working as well as in support of new business activity.  
You’ll report to our COO and work alongside the heads of Design, Technology, Strategy, Business Development, People, IT and Finance.

What you'll do

**Build one discipline out of two.**Product and Delivery here have different histories and different instincts about what great looks like, and both bring real craft with them. Your job is to find what genuinely gets stronger when they come together, then build the discipline around that: its proposition, its craft standards and the shape of the team. Most of the people in it will be hybrid product delivery practitioners, with some leaning one way when a piece of work calls for it, though that balance is something you’ll work out with them rather than inherit from us. This is change work as much as product work, so expect to spend real time on the human side of it. You'll have budget to bring in new people where the discipline needs capability it doesn't have yet, and we'd expect you to be hiring inside the first three months rather than waiting for a perfect picture.  
  
**Own how engagements run.**You’re accountable for how work across the discipline gets shaped, priced and delivered, and you’ll be hands on where it counts, in the shaping, on the engagements that matter most and whenever a team needs you. That includes the harder parts: scope moving, a stakeholder changing their mind late, a plan that needs rebuilding in a week. You’ll hold the commercial performance of the work your discipline runs.  
  
**Set what great looks like.**You’ll define how ustwo does product. How we frame a problem, run customer development, decide what to build first, instrument it so we can see what happened and act on the answer. Roadmaps that survive contact with reality, stories a team can build from, and measurement that tells a client something real about their business. Rigour without bureaucracy is the aim, so bring judgement about how much process a given engagement needs.  
  
**Lead and grow the team.**You’re accountable for the craft of this team and how quickly they’re getting better at it. You’ll set a clear bar, give people honest feedback close to the moment rather than saving it for a review, and back them properly while they grow into more. Where someone consistently isn’t where the role needs them to be, you’ll deal with it fairly and without letting it drift. Hiring, progression and what each level means are yours to define.  
  
**Help us win, and represent ustwo.**You’ll be in pitches, shaping approaches and explaining to clients how we’d tackle their problem. You’ll build senior relationships on live accounts and spot where an engagement could go further than the brief. We’d also like you out in the industry with a point of view worth listening to, in whatever format suits you.  
  
**Keep us ahead of where the craft is going.**AI has changed what a small team can do and how fast, and it’s still moving. You’ll bring a clear view of where it genuinely improves product delivery, then put tooling and practice into the team systematically enough that the effect shows up in the work. More widely, you’ll build a team that treats learning as part of the job.

What we're looking for

**You’ve shipped real products.**From customer development and early discovery through to first release, and you stayed for the stretch afterwards where a product really becomes good. You can talk credibly about the things you got wrong.  
  
**You’ve shaped engagements as well as run them.** Scoping an approach, pricing it, then leading a team to the outcome the client was paying for. You know how scope moves and what to do when a senior stakeholder wants something the plan can’t absorb.  
  
**You speak engineer and designer fluently.**You don't need to have been either, but you do need to hold your own in a trade-off conversation about technical approach. Same with design: you can read a critique properly and you know which decisions aren't yours.  
  
**You’re properly data literate.**You know which numbers tell you something for a given product and which ones are decoration. Retention, acquisition cost, lifetime value and how they connect to a client's business case are familiar territory rather than someone else's job.  
  
**You know how the tooling fits together.** Event taxonomies, analytics and experimentation tooling, and how it's wired up so a team can see what users are doing. Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog or whatever a client runs. You don't need to build it, you need to know when it's telling you the wrong thing.  
  
**You have a point of view on AI in product delivery, and evidence behind it.**Tooling and practice you've put into a team systematically, and a clear account of what it changed about their pace. You know where probabilistic systems behave differently from deterministic ones and what that means for how you design, test and set client expectations.  
  
**You decide without waiting for certainty.**Much of this role happens before the answer is obvious. You look for where an engagement could go further, you shape the offer rather than waiting to be asked, and you change your mind in public when new evidence turns up.  
  
**People want to follow you into it.**You can hold a room, bring a sceptical team along with a change they didn’t ask for, and coach individuals through it. You’re also willing to have the harder conversations early, because letting a performance problem sit is unfair on everyone including the person.  
  
**You’re credible in front of clients.**You can shape and present an approach in a pitch, handle a senior stakeholder who disagrees with you and build the sort of relationship that brings the next piece of work.  
  
**You’ve worked in a product studio, agency or consultancy, and also closer to a single product.**Ideally both, though we care more about the range in your judgement than a line on your CV. Studio life teaches you commercial reality; startup or in-house teaches you what it feels like to live with your own decisions for years.  
  
**You hold a high bar for craft, and you’re curious.**You know what great looks like and you’re honest when work isn’t there yet, in a way that makes people want to go again. You follow what’s changing without being told to, and you build teams where that’s normal.  
  
**What success looks like**  
  
We won't judge this on the performance of any single project. You'll be measured on the commercial performance of the work your discipline runs, and on how our clients and your own team feel about it.  
  
**In your first few weeks** you'll have met everyone in the discipline, and by around six weeks we'd like a clear point of view on where the two crafts are strong, where they're struggling and the direction Product Delivery should take. Not a finished operating model, that comes later, but a direction people recognise themselves in and want to get behind. We'll make sure you have the access to move at that speed. We'd also expect you to be hiring inside the first three months.  
  
**By six months** the discipline should be clear to the people in it. What it stands for, how we cast teams, what each level means and who leads what, settled and communicated properly rather than left to be worked out. Clarity is what lets people move at pace, so we'd rather you got there early and adjusted later than waited until every answer was perfect. By then we'd also expect new people you've brought in to be landing, real change in how teams work visible on live engagements rather than described in a document, and the commercial performance of your discipline's work to be genuinely yours.  
  
**By the end of the first year, we’d expect:**  

* New ways of working that have become the normal way rather than the new thing
* Teams and leaders who deliver well without you in the room, with progression and performance handled openly
* Engagements shaped and priced well, then run in a way that protects both the client outcome and our commercial performance
* Client work that gets measured properly, so we can show what changed and not just what shipped
* AI genuinely built into how the discipline works day to day, with something to point at as evidence
* Senior client relationships that you own and that are opening doors
* A proposition our clients understand and choose us for

  
The bigger prize is a point of view on product that carries. Clear enough inside ustwo that teams actually use it and sharp enough outside that it shapes how other people think, built for where this industry is heading rather than where it has been. We want clients to choose us because of that point of view, and to stay because of what it's like to work with us once they've experienced it.  
  
The honest test is whether the discipline can do things a year from now that it simply couldn't before you arrived.

Why ustwo

We’re employee-owned, which means the people who do the work own the business and share in what it makes. We’re also a B Corp, so how we treat our people, our clients and the world around us is something we’re measured against rather than something we say.  
  
We’re wholly independent too. No parent group setting your targets or holding a view on what your discipline should be, which makes what Product Delivery becomes a genuinely open question rather than a decision taken somewhere else.  
  
Bringing product and delivery together properly is something plenty of studios talk about and very few actually do. You’d be the person doing it, with real room to shape it rather than inheriting someone else’s plan, working alongside the heads of the other disciplines on work that ends up in a lot of people’s hands.

Salary range

* 130,000 – 155,000 GBP Annual
* **Remuneration**  
    
  The salary banding for this role in London is £130,000 to £155,000 depending on experience. Our full benefits package is available to all permanent employees.  
    
  **Applying**  
  Interested but think your experience doesn’t perfectly align with this job description? That’s ok. Research shows underrepresented groups in particular are less inclined to apply for jobs where they don’t meet 100% of the requirements listed. We’d still love to hear from you if you feel passionate about this role. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for our colleagues, clients, community, and the users of our products. We don’t have all the answers but we’re learning together.  
    
  If there’s anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us and we’ll sort it.

This analysis plays a critical role in shaping the security updates that are deployed to customers around the world.
Our research projects cover a wide range of topics, including vulnerability discovery and automation, exploit and vulnerability mitigations, exploit development, operating system security (Windows and Linux), virtualization security, and hardware vulnerabilities and mitigations.
This is a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on improving security for customers worldwide while tackling interesting, real-world security challenges. You will work alongside talented security researchers in a supportive and collaborative environment that encourages innovation, continuous learning, and professional growth.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Analyze critical security vulnerabilities reported by security researchers from around the world and provide guidance on remediation.
Detect, reverse engineer and patch live exploits reported to MSRC.
Use state of the art AI tooling to find and analyze vulnerabilities at scale.
Develop new tools and techniques to improve vulnerability analysis workflows.
Innovate in security mitigations to make Microsoft products and services more resilient to attacks.

Work with and learn from experts across Microsoft and grow your career in security in a motivated and supportive team.

As we prepare for our next phase of growth and innovation, we have an incredibly exciting opportunity for a **Finance Analyst - Operations** to join our Finance Team based in Park Royal.

**The Role:**

This is an analytical role, not a reporting role. Periodic reporting is produced elsewhere within the Finance team, and the focus of this position is to go beyond the numbers to understand what drives restaurant performance and identify opportunities to increase revenue, improve profitability and reduce costs.

Working closely with Operations, the Finance Analyst will analyse P&L, trading, labour and cost data to identify and quantify actionable business opportunities, providing clear insights and recommendations and supporting their implementation through to delivery.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Restaurants profitability and P&L insight**

* Dig into Restaurants and estate P&L performance to identify the underlying drivers of profit, rather than restating the variances.
* Benchmark restaurants against each other to understand what the best performers do differently, and quantify the value of closing the gap.
* Identify structurally underperforming restaurants and build the analysis to support decisions on their future.

**Labour and operational efficiency**

* Analyse labour deployment against sales by Restaurants, day and daypart to find productivity opportunities.
* Work with Operations to test rota, labour model and opening hours changes, and measure the impact.
* Understand the operational drivers of cost and translate them into practical recommendations Area Managers can act on.

**Margin, COGS and waste**

* Investigate gross margin leakage, including waste, stock variances, shrinkage and production over or under ordering.
* Identify and size COGS improvement opportunities with Procurement and Food teams, tracking the benefit through to the P&L.
* Analyse the profitability of products, ranges and dayparts at Restaurants level.

**Restaurants running costs**

* Challenge Restaurants overheads such as utilities, repairs and maintenance, packaging and consumables, finding savings and testing their delivery.

**Commercial and investment analysis**

* Build business cases for operational initiatives, including new equipment, process changes, refits and new restaurants, with clear payback and return on investment.
* Carry out post-investment reviews to check whether initiatives delivered what was promised.
* Support trading analysis on range, pricing and promotions, with a focus on the impact on Restaurants profitability.

**Business partnering**

* Act as the finance partner to Operations, bringing insight and challenge to performance conversations.
* Track agreed opportunities and hold the business to account for delivering them.
* Build strong relationships across Operations, Property, Purchasing and the wider finance team.

About Wellio
Every young person deserves access to quality wellbeing education, regardless of which school they attend or where they live. But schools face an enormous challenge. Teachers are being asked to do more to support student wellbeing, while school leaders need better ways to understand what's working and where students need support. At Wellio, we're working to change that. 

We're building a Wellbeing Management System that brings the best of student wellbeing practice into one platform. From curriculum-aligned lessons and planning tools to student surveys and insights, we're helping schools make wellbeing a consistent and measurable part of everyday learning. And we're growing fast. 

Today, more than 1,000 schools, 25,000 teachers and 210,000 students use Wellio across 25 countries. We're on track for our fourth consecutive year of 100% growth. Our ambition? 50,000 schools. 25 million students. 50 countries. It's a big goal, and there's still an enormous amount to build. That's what makes this such an exciting time to join us.
The role
Wellio is hiring a Senior Product Manager, based in Europe. Until now our founders have shared product leadership. You'll take over ownership of product vision, discovery and delivery across both our platform and our content.

We're a (mostly) bootstrapped company funded by real customers. We like working on real problems that schools couldn't solve on their own. We like to ship fast without letting quality slip.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set strategy and also do the work yourself: shaping pitches, running betting tables and making sure we ship quality work every cycle.

The Work
We're inspired by product philosophies from 37signals, Linear and Airbnb, and we use Shape Up to guide our product development. We believe in small, senior teams that embrace constraints, focus on craft and deliver exceptional outcomes.
Some principles that guide us: continuous discovery, small teams over big ones, embracing constraints, fixed appetites with flexible scopes, knowing our tools and cutting with the grain, treating product as a marketing job, obsessing over craft and sweating the details, and avoiding long-term plans in favour of betting on what matters right now.
Improving student wellbeing needs technology and content that work together seamlessly. Most edtech companies split this work, with platform teams in one place, content teams in another and design somewhere else. We think that leads to narrow solutions that miss the bigger picture. At Wellio, design and content report into product, because the best solutions combine all three.

Day to day, you'll: 
Discover. Spend real time with customers. Watch teachers use Wellio in classrooms, run discovery calls, and explore new markets like primary schools and Indonesia to learn what needs to change.
Set the vision. Work out how schools will run on the first Wellbeing Management System. Distil best practice and show how our platform and content make it work at scale.
Shape and bet. Write pitches that make the problem clear and bring customer pain to life, whether it's a new lesson type, a feature or a whole product line. Work with engineering, design and content so each pitch is a good deal for its appetite, deliverable and usable. Then run the betting tables that lock in the next eight weeks of work for platform and content.
Ship. Keep projects within their appetite. You'll wield the scope hammer and stop work from dragging on forever. You'll also hold the quality line and refuse to ship mediocre work just because "we promised it" or "we spent time on it".
Close the loop. After launch, use interviews, data and usage to check that what we built actually helps, then iterate.
Tell the story. We see product partly as a marketing job. As the person closest to the product and the problem, you'll shape the messaging that sales and marketing use.

About you 
You have experience in product management and helped scale B2B SaaS products. You love well-crafted tools of any kind.
You spot opportunities and problems early, and your discovery is excellent. You dig into a customer’s real pain and build what they couldn’t have imagined.
You know content, design and engineering well enough to go deep with each, and you could write a lesson, mock up a flow in Figma or build a simple Rails feature yourself. You make customer problems feel real to the team and you hold the line on quality.
You care about outcomes, not output. No decks or status updates for their own sake: you turn problems into pitches, prototypes and shipped changes, and judge your work by what changed for schools.
You ship with AI every day. Our designer and co-founder both ship features, and you will too, with our engineers reviewing your work rather than doing it for you.
You’re based in Europe. Most of our schools and team are in Australia, so you’re comfortable working async with a few early calls each week. You’ll be close to our UK schools and London base, and travel a couple of times a year to see the team.

Why You Should Work Here
Build something from the ground up. You'll be our first Product Marketing Manager and a foundational member of our growing marketing team. You'll have the opportunity to shape a function that will play an increasingly important role in Wellio's future.
Join at an exciting stage of growth. We're growing rapidly, expanding our platform and investing in the people who will help take Wellio to the next level. There's a huge opportunity to make a meaningful contribution and grow with the business.
Make an impact around the world. Your work won't be limited to one market. You'll help schools across Australia, the UK and internationally discover and get more value from Wellio, contributing to better wellbeing education for young people around the world.
Work alongside people who've scaled. You'll work with a Head of Marketing who led B2B growth at Canva, experienced product and sales leaders, and founders who are deeply involved in building the business.
High standards, low ego, and a global team. We care deeply about our mission and the quality of our work, but we don't take ourselves too seriously. We value transparency, flexibility and strong relationships. We also bring our global team together for gatherings in places like London and Bangkok to plan, connect and have a great time together. 
If you're excited by the opportunity to build something from scratch, help shape a fast-growing global company and make a difference in schools around the world, we'd love to hear from you.

* Diagnose faults across subsystem boundaries: propulsion and powertrain (motors, ESCs, props, batteries, thrust, thermal, vibration); flight control (stability, tuning, actuator limits, control allocation, mode transitions, failsafes); and navigation and state estimation (IMUs, GNSS, compasses, barometers, RTK, sensor fusion, estimator health).

The Deputy/SENCo will contribute to the management of the day-to-day operations of Out of School Childcare & Play services and ancillary play projects at a designated Playcentre, and to fulfil the role of named SENCo for the setting. 3. Ensure all services are planned and delivered in line with PACE policies and procedures, statutory obligations, legal frameworks and the contractual requirements of funders.

6. Work in partnership with other PACE teams and staff, and liaise effectively with parents, carers, professionals, external agencies and other relevant individuals as appropriate.
7. Build, maintain and strengthen partnerships within the local community to promote understanding, improve access to resources and create a broad range of opportunities for children, young people and their families.

9. Work with the Senior Centre Manager to ensure that the building, playground and resources are well maintained, safe, fit for purpose and suitable for the needs of the children and young people using the service.

20. Promote and publicise services effectively so that they are accessible to all sections of the community.

22. Undertake training and professional development as required to fulfil the responsibilities of the role.
23. Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role as required from time to time.

1. **Experience and qualifications**

  

An appropriate early years, childcare, education or play work qualification at NVQ level 3 or above that meets the standards required by Ofsted & EYFS registration and inspection processes.

Experience of managing staff and leading teams in delivering high quality, inclusive play or childcare service.

Significant experience of working with disabled children, young people and parents/carers and of facilitating an inclusive child-centred service.

Experience of working in partnership with other agencies and organisations.

A thorough knowledge and understanding of the EYFS, Ofsted standards and relevant current legislation.

Knowledge and understanding of safeguarding policies and procedures and experience of partnership working.

Thorough knowledge of child development.

Knowledge of the needs of children with SEN – gained through experience.

Awareness of effective strategies and techniques.

Knowledge of the SEN Code of Practice.
